The Manager, IT Supplier Management is responsible for leading ALSAC's Information Technology supplier management function, overseeing the strategy, governance, performance, and commercial management of technology suppliers across software, SaaS, cloud, infrastructure, telecommunications, consulting, and managed services.

This role serves as a key partner to IT leadership, Finance, Procurement, Legal, Information Security, and business stakeholders to ensure supplier relationships deliver measurable business value, support organizational priorities, mitigate risk, and optimize technology investments.

The Manager will lead both strategic and operational supplier management activities, including vendor selection, RFx processes, contract negotiations, renewals, performance management, supplier governance, spend optimization, and supplier relationship management. This leader will drive the continued maturity of ALSAC's IT supplier management practices while ensuring effective execution of day-to-day supplier operations.

This position is ideal for a collaborative leader who combines strong business acumen, negotiation expertise, relationship management skills, and technology industry knowledge to deliver exceptional supplier outcomes.

What You'll Do

Strategic Supplier Leadership

  • Develop, implement, and continuously improve IT supplier management policies, standards, processes, and governance practices.
  • Drive supplier management maturity, operational efficiencies, and technology spend optimization initiatives.
  • Establish supplier performance measurement frameworks, scorecards, reporting, and supplier tiering models.
  • Evaluate market trends and supplier capabilities to support strategic technology decisions.

Vendor Relationship Management

  • Lead strategic relationships with technology suppliers, consulting partners, and service providers.
  • Conduct regular business reviews and hold suppliers accountable for contractual obligations, service levels, performance commitments, and business outcomes.
  • Manage supplier escalations, dispute resolution, and performance improvement initiatives.
  • Foster collaborative supplier partnerships while maintaining strong governance and accountability.

Contract, Sourcing & Commercial Management

  • Lead vendor evaluations, RFx activities, supplier selection processes, and contract negotiations.
  • Negotiate pricing, commercial terms, service-level agreements (SLAs), renewals, Statements of Work (SOWs), and other supplier agreements.
  • Partner with Procurement, Legal, Finance, and Information Security to ensure contracts align with organizational requirements and mitigate risk.
  • Identify opportunities to consolidate suppliers, optimize licensing, and increase purchasing leverage.

Financial & Risk Management

  • Monitor supplier spend, budgeting inputs, forecasting activities, and invoice management processes.
  • Identify cost savings, cost avoidance, and value optimization opportunities across the technology portfolio.
  • Evaluate supplier financial viability, operational performance, and market conditions to proactively mitigate risk.
  • Maintain supplier risk, performance, and spend data to support business decision-making.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate closely with IT leadership, Project Management Office, Finance, Procurement, Legal, Information Security, and business stakeholders.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor on supplier strategy, contract management, sourcing approaches, and vendor governance.
  • Support technology initiatives by ensuring supplier engagements align with organizational objectives, policies, and standards.
  • Deliver training, guidance, and best practices related to supplier management across IT.

Team Leadership

  • Provide leadership, coaching, prioritization, and development for IT Supplier Management team members.
  • Oversee execution of supplier management services and operational processes.
  • Promote a culture of accountability, customer service, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree and 6 year's experience, including managerial experience.
  • Experience developing and managing IT supplier management policies, standards, governance frameworks, and operational processes.
  • Experience managing technology suppliers across software, SaaS, cloud, telecommunications, infrastructure, consulting, and managed services.
  • Demonstrated expertise in supplier relationship management, vendor performance management, and supplier governance.
  • Proven success leading complex technology contract negotiations and working directly with internal and external legal counsel.
  • Experience managing RFx processes, supplier evaluations, supplier selection, and contract lifecycle activities.
  • Experience establishing supplier performance metrics, scorecards, and executive reporting.
  • Strong financial acumen with experience supporting budgeting, forecasting, invoice review, spend analysis, and cost optimization.
  • Experience defining, negotiating, and enforcing service-level agreements (SLAs).
  • Strong analytical, organizational, project management, and problem-solving skills.

The Senior Data Modeler designs and evolves high-quality data models across our modern data platform. This role combines strong hands-on modeling expertise with growing involvement in AI-forward data practices—including semantic layers, enriched metadata, and structured data descriptions that enable AI systems to work with enterprise data effectively.

This position will operate as a key contributor within the Data Engineering team, translating business requirements into well-governed logical and physical models that serve analytics, reporting, and emerging AI use cases. While architectural strategy and enterprise standards are set by the Principal Data Engineer and VP of Data Engineering, it will be a critical partner in executing that vision—bringing strong modeling judgment, cross-system awareness, and a willingness to engage with modern semantic and AI-adjacent concepts.

This is not a narrow, single-project role. This position thinks across the data lifecycle—from systems of record through the lakehouse to downstream consumers—and who can grow into increasing ownership of semantic and AI-ready data design over time.

Outcome and Activities

  • This position will work from home; occasional planned travel to an assigned Southfield, Michigan office location may be required.  However, this position is permitted to work at a Southfield, Michigan office location if requested by the team member
  • Data Modeling and Design: Design and maintain logical and physical data models (dimensional, relational) across our Databricks lakehouse environment. Apply Kimball star schema and normalized modeling best practices. Translate business requirements into clear, well-documented data structures that serve analytics, reporting, and AI consumption.
  • Cross-System Data Lifecycle Awareness: Model data with awareness of the full lifecycle—from systems of record through integration layers to lakehouse and downstream consumers. Ensure models account for how data originates, flows, and is consumed across multiple systems, not just within the big data platform.
  • Semantic Layer and AI-Ready Data: Support the development of semantic layer artifacts (curated views, conformed dimensions, governed metrics, Genie-ready configurations) that enable AI agents and self-service analytics to interpret enterprise data correctly. Partner with the Principal Data Engineer to evolve metadata practices toward richer, machine-interpretable descriptions—business definitions, relationships, and constraints.
  • Metadata and Business Glossary: Contribute to critical data element identification, business glossary development, and data dictionary maintenance. Help explore approaches to reduce manual cataloging effort through AI-assisted tooling and programmatic metadata generation.
  • Collaboration and Delivery: Partner with data engineers to implement models in performant ELT pipelines and denormalized views (such as Dealer Datahub patterns). Participate in design reviews, provide modeling guidance during development, and work cross-functionally with business stakeholders and analytics teams.
  • Governance and Standards: Adhere to and help refine enterprise data modeling standards, naming conventions, and design patterns within the SDLC. Support model review processes, change management, and data quality efforts. Identify opportunities to improve modeling approaches or reduce duplication.

Competencies: The following items detail how you will be successful in this role.

  • Customer Empathy: Customer Empathy is the ability to understand the perspectives, pain points, and experiences of customers. It involves actively putting oneself in the customer’s shoes, comprehending their needs and challenges, and using that understanding to provide a better, more customer-centric experience.
  • Engineering Excellence: Engineering Excellence is about bringing great craftsmanship and thought leadership to deliver an outstanding product that delights customers and solves for the business. This involves the pursuit and achievement of high standards, best practices, innovation, and superior solutions.
  • One Team: A One Team mindset refers to a collaborative approach across the organization, where individuals work together seamlessly, without boundaries, as a single, cohesive team. Shared goals, open communication and mutual support create a sense of collective purpose. This enables teams to navigate challenges and pursue shared objectives more effectively.
  • Owner’s Mindset: Owner’s Mindset involves adopting a set of behaviors that reflect a sense of responsibility, accountability, strategic thinking, and a proactive approach to managing your domain. As an owner, you understand the business and your domain(s) deeply and solve for the right outcome for the domain(s) and the business.

  • 8+ years of experience in data modeling, data architecture, or analytics engineering roles
  • Strong hands-on expertise in dimensional modeling (Kimball) and relational modeling (3NF)
  • Experience modeling data across multiple source systems in cloud data platforms (Databricks or similar)
  • Awareness of how data models serve downstream AI and analytics use cases, with willingness to deepen expertise in semantic layer design and AI-ready data structures
  • Proficient SQL skills and experience working closely with data engineers on ELT pipelines
  • Experience with data modeling and design tools (ER/Studio, ERwin, SqlDBM, dbt, or similar)
  • Understanding of data governance concepts including lineage, metadata management, and data quality
  • Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate across technical and business teams
  • Self-directed and comfortable operating with autonomy while working within established architectural direction
  • Experience with or exposure to semantic layers, governed metrics, or analytics modeling frameworks

Preferred:

  • Familiarity with metadata management platforms, data catalogs, or data documentation tools (e.g., Collibra, Unity Catalog)
  • Awareness of knowledge graphs, ontologies, or formal data description frameworks (OWL, RDF)—deep expertise not required, but curiosity and willingness to learn is essential

  • Exposure to AI-assisted tooling for metadata, documentation, or data profiling tasks

jobDescription:
The State Street Investment Management’s (IM) Business & Technology Risk and Resilience (BTRR) team is first line function that partners with business teams to properly manage operational, technology, and regulatory risk, together with business and technology resiliency. Business Risk Partners within BTRR are aligned to both IM business functions, and specific regions to ensure appropriate coverage for our global operating model. They act as operational risk experts to advise business stakeholders on the execution of risk programs and support their ongoing requirement to identify, assess and mitigate operational risk. This role will specifically serve as the Investments Business Partner. Seeking professional with 10+ years of experience in operational risk, compliance or audit with a focus on risk assessment, monitoring, and effective program design and leadership.

As the COO - Investments Business Risk Partner, you will:

  • Maintain deep subject matter knowledge related to business line control activities, operating model, strategy, and key initiatives; efficiently and effectively apply this insight into how content, themes, and priorities are framed and actioned.
  • Establish and maintain productive relationships with key business function leaders; instill confidence by demonstrating credibility and expertise on core programs and services to influence outcomes.

  • Review and challenge Incident and Issue content as part of the Reviewer stage of the workflow to ensure proper alignment between root cause, risk materiality / likelihood, and any required corrective or preventative action.
  • Lead the Risk & Controls Self-Assessment execution workshops to determine and rationalize the inherent risk ratings and controls effectiveness ratings for risks applicable to the Business Unit. Guide the business through the re-designed RCSA process alignment, including completion of process mapping.
  • Perform regular trend analysis on incidents and issues to identify common themes in root cause and areas of focus for deep dive risk assessments with recommendations to the business on control enhancements.
  • Assist the business line in addressing findings and potential risk exposures identified by SLOD Operational Risk and Compliance, TLOD Corporate Audit, external audit and regulators.
  • Maintain regular touchpoints with SLOD and TLOD to coordinate risk assessments and validate consistency in our evaluations of each business line’s overall risk posture.
  • Participate in new product launches and new processes implementation projects to offer expertise in identifying risk exposures and assist the business line in suitably designing controls to mitigate such risks.
  • Conduct status meetings with business line partners to discuss open incidents and issues, and identify emerging risks requiring attention. Direct inquiries from business partners to BTRR framework partners, where appropriate.

These skills will help you succeed in this role:

  • 10+ years of financial services experience with a large financial services firm or advisory/consulting firm including experience as an internal auditor, public accountant, risk or compliance officer
  • Experience in risk management, regulatory compliance, or control programs
  • Knowledge of common risk management frameworks and methodologies
  • Independent strategic thinker with an understanding of regulatory, operational, and technology risks in financial services, preferably within investment management function(s)

ETF as a Service – VP – State Street Investment Management

Location: London, United Kingdom

Business Unit: State Street Investment Management

Reporting Line: Reports to Global Head of ETF as a Service

BUILDING THE NEXT GENERATION OF ETF MANUFACTURING

ETF as a Service has moved beyond a high growth phase to become a core, institutional, global platform within State Street Investment Management. As the business scales its third‑party ETF manufacturing capabilities across jurisdictions, we are hiring a Vice President to play a critical leadership role in industrializing onboarding, managing client relationships, enforcing pricing and margin discipline, and driving consistent, high‑quality launch execution globally.

This is a senior execution and platform‑building role, with accountability for outcomes rather than tasks. The VP will operate at the intersection of product structuring, commercial discipline, operating model design, client service, and cross‑functional orchestration, acting as a senior owner across complex launches and platform initiatives.

What You Will Do

  • Own and evolve global launch and onboarding frameworks, including the design and continuous improvement of structured, scalable onboarding playbooks

  • Lead complex ETF launches across US and international markets, acting as a senior execution owner and escalation point

  • Drive cross‑functional orchestration across funds management, legal, compliance, capital markets, operations, and technology, ensuring clarity of ownership and delivery discipline

  • Lead business development for ETF as a Service mandates, with accountability for structuring, and converting opportunities in partnership with distribution and senior leadership, bringing platform, pricing, and execution leadership throughout the sales and onboarding lifecycle

  • Develop and manage senior client relationships post mandate win, acting as a trusted partner across launch, scale, and evolution phases, and ensuring a consistent, high quality client experience across regions and functions

  • Set and enforce execution standards, improving launch consistency, timeline discipline, and predictability at scale

  • Monitor cost of manufacturing and operational efficiency, identifying improvement levers and supporting informed commercial decisions

  • Lead the development and adoption of standardized pricing frameworks across regions and client segments

  • Drive the industrialization of platform infrastructure, processes, and controls to support global scale

  • Own contributions to standardized documentation, governance frameworks, and decision templates

  • Identify structural bottlenecks and execution risk, proposing and driving scalable, sustainable improvements

  • Act as a trusted partner to senior stakeholders, influencing outcomes and balancing commercial, operational, and risk considerations

Who We Are Looking For

  • Typically 7+ years of relevant experience in ETF product, investment management, capital markets, platform operations, digital wealth, or top tier consulting

  • Experience operating across multiple regulatory frameworks, including UCITS and 40 Act ETF structures, is strongly preferred

  • Demonstrated experience owning complex cross‑functional initiatives within a global or multi‑jurisdictional environment

  • Deep exposure to ETF structures, fund launches, pricing models, or platform economics

  • Strong commercial judgment with advanced analytical and financial modelling capability

  • Proven track record in delivering client solutions and managing strategic client engagements

  • Highly structured thinker with the ability to operate effectively in fast moving environments

  • Proven capability to lead senior stakeholders, influence decisions, and drive alignment without formal authority

What Makes This Role Attractive

  • Senior ownership of real ETF launches in multiple jurisdictions, strategic client relationships and complex structuring decisions at global scale

  • Direct involvement in shaping pricing, margin, governance, and operating model frameworks

  • Opportunity to help define how a major asset manager industrializes ETF manufacturing for third‑party clients

  • High visibility role with meaningful impact on platform strategy, scale, and commercial sustainability

  • This role is part of a strategic priority for the firm, with significant visibility and long-term career upside.

Success Looks Like

  • Measurable improvement in launch consistency and execution discipline across all regions

  • Strong credibility and rigor in pricing, margin analysis, and commercial decision making

  • Scalable onboarding frameworks embedded across regions and teams

  • Clear demonstration of end‑to‑end ownership across complex, high‑stakes execution environments

jobTitle: IGA Operations and Support Lead - VP
jobDescription:
Who we are looking for

State Street Identity and Access Management is looking for outstanding individuals with
excellent intellectual and analytical capabilities, entrepreneurial problem-solving skills, strong
communications, and influencing capabilities. This role will have a broad range of responsibilities within IAM/IGA.

This role can be performed in a hybrid model, where you can balance work from home and office to match your needs and role requirements.

Title: IGA Operations and Support Leader

Job Description: The IGA Operations and Support Leader is accountable for the reliable, secure and efficient operation of enterprise identity governance services. The role unifies platform run, access operations, governance operations and service excellence under one operating model while preserving control ownership, service continuity and 24x7 coverage where required.

Key Responsibilities

Operational Leadership & Service Management

• Provide single-point accountability across Platform Run, Access Operations, Governance Operations and Service Excellence; lead tower owners through common governance, service ownership and escalation.

• Establish a common service catalogue, intake and priority model, SLAs, scorecard and escalation path; oversee incident, problem, request, change, release, capacity, disaster recovery and service continuity.

• Drive backlog health, root-cause elimination, cross-training and reduction of duplicate handoffs across five support towers and approximately 78 resources.

Platform & Access Operations

• Ensure stable and secure operation of SailPoint, integrations, connectors, batch processing and supporting infrastructure, including L1-L3 support, monitoring and production controls.

• Oversee joiner, mover and leaver administration, provisioning, deprovisioning, queues, reconciliation and exception management.

• Lead operational support for certifications, roles, entitlements, segregation of duties, control execution, evidence production and access reporting.

Service Excellence, Risk & Vendor Management

• Define consistent measures for demand, SLAs, backlog, quality, risk, capacity, automation and customer experience; increase self-service and automate high-volume manual work.

• Maintain audit readiness through clear control ownership, traceable evidence, timely issue management and sustainable remediation.

• Own workforce planning, budget inputs and vendor governance; act as the senior operational interface for technology, cybersecurity, business, application, risk and control stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Cybersecurity or a related field, or equivalent experience; Master's degree preferred.

• 10+ years in IAM, cybersecurity operations or enterprise technology operations, including significant leadership responsibility in a complex, controlled environment.

• Deep knowledge of identity lifecycle operations, provisioning, access certification, roles, entitlements, segregation of duties and reconciliation.

• Leadership experience with SailPoint IdentityIQ, IdentityNow or an equivalent enterprise IGA platform.

• Strong command of IT service management, operational resilience, production controls, change governance, service measurement, audit and regulatory commitments.

• Experience leading internal teams and third-party providers through service stabilization, transformation and continuous improvement.

Preferred Qualifications

• CISSP, CISM, CISA, ITIL or vendor-specific IGA certification; financial-services or other highly regulated industry experience.

• Knowledge of ServiceNow, workflow automation, operational analytics, PAM, authentication, zero trust, cloud identity and scripting.

Key Competencies

Enterprise operational leadership and service ownership. Risk and control mindset. Data-driven decision-making. Executive communication and stakeholder influence. Vendor, financial, transformation and talent leadership.

Success Metrics

• Reliability, availability, recovery and SLA performance; healthy backlog and lower incident recurrence.

• Accurate and timely provisioning, certification and control execution; sustainable remediation supported by complete evidence.

• Greater automation, fewer handoffs, consistent scorecard adoption, stakeholder satisfaction and effective vendor performance.

Our technology function, Global Technology Services (GTS), is vital to State Street and is the key enabler for our business to deliver data and insights to our clients. Who we are looking for 

State Street is seeking a Security Platform Governance & Resilience Lead for our Security Platforms team, which is part of the State Street Cyber Fusion Center. The Security Platforms team designs, manages and supports the security technologies that enable cybersecurity operations across State Street. These platforms are critical to the firm's security posture, enabling threat detection, incident response, threat hunting, vulnerability management, data protection, automation and other key cybersecurity functions.  

This role will be responsible for driving governance, operational resilience, service management, process maturity and performance management across the Security Platforms portfolio. The successful candidate will partner closely with platform engineering, security operations, risk, compliance, audit and regulatory stakeholders to ensure security platforms remain resilient, well governed, measurable and audit ready. 

Success in this role will require strong operational leadership, governance expertise, stakeholder management skills and a solid understanding of cybersecurity operations and supporting technologies. 

What you will be responsible for 

As Security Platform Governance & Resilience Lead, you will: 

  • Establish and maintain governance processes across the Security Platforms organisation. 
  • Develop and manage platform health, operational performance and resilience metrics. 
  • Create executive, operational and management reporting for platform services. 
  • Own governance of platform roadmaps, strategic initiatives and service improvement programmes. 
  • Build and operate demand intake, prioritisation and governance processes for Security Platforms. 
  • Coordinate audit, regulatory examination and compliance activities affecting the platform portfolio. 
  • Establish repeatable evidence collection processes supporting internal and external audits. 
  • Develop, maintain and continuously improve platform SOPs, standards, control documentation and operating procedures. 
  • Drive operational resilience planning, testing and continuous improvement activities. 
  • Partner with platform engineering teams to improve operational maturity and consistency across services. 
  • Identify, track and drive remediation of operational risks, issues and control gaps. 
  • Develop service management practices including KPIs, SLAs, service reviews and continual improvement programmes. 
  • Coordinate governance activities across Cyber Defence, Incident Response, Detection Engineering, Identity & Access Management, Risk Management, Compliance and Internal Audit teams. 
  • Support leadership decision-making through meaningful metrics, dashboards and performance reporting. 
  • Promote a culture of operational excellence, accountability and continuous improvement. 

 

What we value 

These skills will help you succeed in this role: 

  • Strong understanding of cybersecurity operations and supporting platform functions. 
  • Experience operating in highly regulated financial services or similarly regulated environments. 
  • Excellent governance, process design and operational management capabilities. 
  • Experience supporting internal audit, regulatory examinations and compliance activities. 
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate operational data into meaningful insights. 
  • Experience developing service health metrics, dashboards and executive reporting. 
  • Understanding of operational resilience, risk management and control frameworks. 
  • Strong programme and stakeholder management skills. 
  • Ability to influence senior stakeholders across technology, cybersecurity and business functions. 
  • Experience building sustainable operating models and scalable governance processes. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills. 
  • Ability to balance operational, regulatory and strategic priorities across a global organisation. 

 

Education & Preferred Qualifications 

  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Information Systems, Business Management or a related discipline is beneficial but not required. 
  • Equivalent practical experience in cybersecurity operations, governance, service management, risk management or technology operations will be considered in lieu of formal education. 
  • 10+ years of experience in cybersecurity, technology operations, governance, risk, compliance or service management functions. 
  • Experience supporting cybersecurity operations, engineering or security platform organisations. 
  • Working knowledge of security technologies such as EDR, SIEM, SOAR, DLP, Identity Security and Cloud Security platforms. 
  • Experience managing audit deliverables, evidence requests and regulatory engagements. 
  • Experience developing governance frameworks, operating models and service management processes. 
  • Familiarity with Archer, ServiceNow, Jira or similar governance and workflow platforms. 
  • Industry certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, ITIL or equivalent are desirable but not required. 

 

Why this role is important to us 

Security Platforms provides and operates many of the foundational technologies used by State Street's Cyber Fusion Center and broader cybersecurity organisation. As our platform portfolio continues to expand in scope, capability and regulatory obligations, maintaining strong governance, operational resilience and service management practices becomes increasingly important.  

The Security Platform Governance & Resilience Lead will help ensure platform services remain scalable, resilient, measurable and aligned with regulatory expectations while enabling engineering teams to focus on delivering secure and reliable cybersecurity capabilities. This role will serve as a key partner to platform leadership, helping drive operational maturity, audit readiness, resilience planning, governance excellence and continual improvement across the Security Platforms function.

We are offering an opportunity to join the Liquidity Management team, supporting the positioning and funding of State Street’s global nostro balances across the EMEA region. The Officer will oversee daily business-as-usual activity, provide direct support to the management team and act as a role model and first point of escalation for the wider team. The role requires clear communication, sound judgement and the ability to remain calm and composed in a highly time-critical environment.

Responsibilities

  • Oversee the Liquidity Management team’s daily BAU activity, ensuring priorities, currency deadlines and operational risks are managed effectively.
  • Provide and oversee forecasts of expected nostro-related cash activity and monitor direct clearing activity.
  • Review and release funding calculations and payments, applying a high level of critical attention to detail.
  • Act as a subject-matter expert and first point of escalation for complex cash-related investigations and operational issues.
  • Provide direct support to the management team, field questions from colleagues and stakeholders, and deliver clear and accurate updates to senior management.
  • Remain calm and composed in pressurised or time-critical situations, making sound and rational decisions.
  • Demonstrate a proactive approach to cash funding and nostro forecasting to maximise net interest revenue and reduce exposure.
  • Maintain awareness of matters affecting cash funding, including foreign exchange and interest-rate volatility.
  • Maintain effective relationships with internal and external counterparts, including Treasury and Cash teams, client service groups, brokers, sub-custodians, agent banks and clearing schemes.
  • Prepare and validate reports for delivery to management.
  • Train team members and provide ongoing operational coaching, while supporting the manager’s wider development objectives.
  • Maintain the team’s operating procedures and ensure they remain accurate and up to date.
  • Deputise for the manager when required.
  • Participate in projects as required, representing the business and ensuring operational requirements are understood.

Skills and Experience

  • At least five years of relevant banking, liquidity or cash management experience.
  • Previous supervisory or team-lead experience is preferred.
  • Strong working knowledge of major financial instruments and products affecting cash flow.
  • Sound understanding of securities transactions, individual market nuances and cash-related market deadlines.
  • Demonstrable experience of reviewing and releasing high-value or time-critical payments and funding activity.
  • Exceptional attention to detail, with the ability to identify, challenge and resolve discrepancies before release.
  • Ability to oversee multiple priorities in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment and provide clear direction where appropriate.
  • Decisive and composed, with demonstrated ability to make sound decisions under pressure.
  • Clear and confident written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to report effectively to senior management.
  • Ability to investigate complex cash issues, explain findings clearly and drive matters through to resolution.
  • Ability to train, coach and act as a positive role model for colleagues.
  • Flexibility in work schedule.
  • Familiarity with AI-enabled tools and an interest in their responsible use to improve productivity and operational efficiency are desirable.
  • Proficient PC skills, with strong Microsoft Excel knowledge desirable.

jobDescription:
Managing Director – Business Risk Advisor Lead

Financing and Portfolio Solutions

Business Risk Management | Markets Risk Advisory

LEVEL
Managing Director

FUNCTION
Business Risk Management

WORK ARRANGEMENT
Hybrid – 4 days in office

Who we are looking for

We are looking for a senior first-line Business Risk executive to lead the risk advisory and control agenda for State Street's Financing and Portfolio Solutions franchise, which includes Agency Lending, Prime Services, Secured Financing and Repo, and Portfolio Solutions businesses. The role will establish strategic direction, provide credible challenge to senior business leaders, and oversee a resilient, regulator-ready control environment across this integrated financing platform.

This Managing Director will lead a team of Business Risk professionals and will partner closely with Front Office, Operations, Technology, Compliance, Legal, Finance, Enterprise Risk and Internal Audit. The successful candidate will balance commercial objectives with disciplined risk management, regulatory compliance, operational resilience, and sustainable execution.

Why this role is important to us

Financing Solutions and Portfolio Solutions operate at the intersection of trading, financing, collateral management and client delivery, where regulatory scrutiny, operational complexity and commercial priorities converge. This role provides executive ownership of the first-line risk framework, helping businesses grow responsibly, innovate confidently, and maintain robust governance, controls and escalation practices.

What you will be responsible for

As the Business Risk Advisor Lead for Financing and Portfolio Solutions, you will:

  • Serve as the senior Business Risk Management lead and principal escalation point for material risk, control and emerging-risk matters affecting Financing Solutions, Portfolio Solutions and adjacent Markets activities.

  • Lead and develop a team of Business Risk professionals, set clear accountability and priorities, and oversee the quality and consistency of risk advisory coverage delivered to the supported businesses.

  • Provide executive-level risk advice and credible challenges to business leadership across trade execution, lifecycle management, financing, collateral, valuation, market conduct, surveillance and regulatory reporting.

  • Establish and oversee the end-to-end first-line risk and control framework, including risk and control assessments, control inventories, key risk indicators, issue management, incident and near-miss governance, and senior management reporting.

  • Ensure material incidents, control failures and emerging exposures are identified early, escalated promptly, investigated thoroughly and remediated through sustainable, well-documented actions.

  • Drive control modernization through automation, data-led monitoring, process simplification and exception-based oversight, with particular focus on reducing manual error and strengthening preventive and detective controls.

  • Lead Business Risk engagement for regulatory examinations, internal audits and independent reviews, including preparation of clear narratives, evidence, management responses and sustainable remediation plans.

  • Partner with Compliance and Legal to assess evolving SEC, FINRA, Federal Reserve, Prudential regulators, and applicable global broker-dealer requirements and translate them into practical business and control actions.

  • Provide executive risk sponsorship and challenge for new products, business expansion, strategic change, technology transformation and operating-model initiatives, including assessment of readiness, scalability and residual risk.

  • Chair or represent the business in relevant risk committees and governance forums, ensuring transparent reporting, timely decisions, clear ownership and disciplined action tracking.

  • Build effective partnerships across the three lines of defense and communicate complex risk matters in clear, decision-ready language for executive leadership, governance committees, auditors and regulators.

  • Promote a strong culture of risk ownership, constructive challenge, accountability and continuous improvement across the supported businesses.

What we value

These skills will help you succeed in this role:

  • Executive presence and the ability to influence, challenge and advise senior leaders while maintaining strong business partnerships.

  • Deep knowledge of first-line risk management, control design, issue and incident management, operational resilience and regulatory remediation.

  • Commercial judgment and the ability to balance business growth with the firm’s risk appetite, regulatory obligations and control standards.

  • Strategic thinking combined with disciplined execution, clear escalation, and strong attention to the quality of risk documentation and evidence.

  • Ability to lead through complexity, set direction across a global stakeholder network, and build high-performing, inclusive teams.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication, including experience presenting to executive committees, governance forums, auditors and regulators.

Education and preferred qualifications

  • 15+ years of financial services experience, including significant senior leadership experience in Business Risk, Markets Risk, Operational Risk, Compliance, Audit, Business Controls or a related function.

  • Direct experience supporting broker-dealers, capital markets, securities finance, prime brokerage, secured financing, portfolio solutions or multi-asset trading businesses.

  • Deep understanding of trade lifecycle processes, market infrastructure, collateral and margin, valuation, regulatory reporting, and front-to-back operating and control models.

  • Demonstrated success leading regulatory examinations, audits, complex remediation programs and large-scale control or operating-model transformation.

  • Proven people leadership experience, including developing senior risk professionals and coordinating teams and stakeholders across regions.

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required; advanced degree and relevant industry or risk certifications are preferred.

This role is responsible for the operational strategy, reliability, resiliency, observability, security operations governance, and operational transformation of the AWS Federated platform. This is not a traditional infrastructure operations leadership role. Instead, the AWS Federated Platform Operations Lead will drive the next generation of cloud operations by leveraging AI, agentic workflows, automation, operational intelligence, reliability engineering, and platform-based support models to improve service quality, reduce operational risk, and accelerate innovation.

The role serves as a key member of the AWS Federated leadership team and will play a pivotal role in shaping the future multi-cloud operating model across State Street.

Key Responsibilities

Define and Execute the Cloud Operations Strategy

  • Develop and execute the long-term operational vision and roadmap for AWS Federated.
  • Establish operational standards, governance frameworks, and service management practices aligned with enterprise objectives.
  • Drive continuous improvement in operational maturity, platform reliability, customer experience, and service quality.
  • Partner with engineering leaders to integrate operability, observability, resiliency, and supportability into platform design decisions.
  • Influence enterprise cloud operating model strategy and operational transformation initiatives.

Lead the Transformation to AI-Powered Operations

  • Drive adoption of Agentic AI capabilities across cloud operations and platform management.

    • Incident correlation

  • Oversee the health and effectiveness of the automated service, including interfaces, exceptions, recurring defects, control results, and operational workarounds.

jobTitle: Balance Sheet and NII Forecast, Assistant Vice President
jobDescription:
Who We Are Looking For

Asset Liability Management (ALM), a division of Global Treasury, is responsible for managing the corporate balance sheet, forecasting Net Interest Income (NII), and overseeing interest rate risk positioning. The team focuses on optimizing the risk-return profile of the balance sheet by developing strategies that sustain and grow NII while operating within regulatory and risk appetite constraints. ALM partners closely with colleagues across Global Treasury, Finance, Risk Management, and business units to support the firm's strategic objectives and balance sheet management framework.

The Assistant Vice President, Balance Sheet & NII Forecasting, will play a key role in shaping the firm's balance sheet and earnings outlook. This candidate will own forecasting workflows and deliverables and collaborate across Treasury, Finance, Risk, and business teams to deliver actionable insights that support strategic decision-making. The role is responsible for producing and communicating balance sheet and Net Interest Income (NII) forecasts, identifying risks and opportunities, and supporting initiatives that influence balance sheet positioning, financial performance, and risk management outcomes.

Why This Role Is Important to Us

The team you will be joining plays a critical role in supporting the financial strength and strategic direction of the organization. Institutional investors around the world rely on us to manage risk, adapt to evolving market conditions, and deliver strong financial performance. Achieving these objectives requires talented professionals who can translate complex financial information into meaningful insights and drive effective decision-making.

In this role, you will help strengthen the firm's balance sheet management capabilities through rigorous analysis, innovative problem solving, and effective stakeholder engagement. You will contribute to a high-performing team that values collaboration, continuous improvement, and operational excellence while supporting critical business and regulatory priorities.

What You Will Be Responsible For

  • Own monthly liability-side of balance sheet and Net Interest Income (NII) forecasting process using Quantitative Risk Management (QRM), incorporating inputs from business units and key stakeholders across the organization.

  • Analyze and communicate the primary drivers of forecast performance, including variances relative to prior forecasts, strategic plans, and actual results.

  • Develop insightful analyses and recommendations to support balance sheet management, funding strategy, hedging and capital allocation, as well as ad-hoc Treasury initiatives.

  • Partner with stakeholders across Treasury, Finance, Risk Management, and business units to identify risks, opportunities, and emerging trends impacting forecast outcomes.

  • Prepare and deliver clear, concise, and executive-ready presentations for senior management, governance forums, and committee meetings.

  • Support quarterly earnings processes by analyzing actual business performance, evaluating forecast accuracy, and providing forward-looking insights.

  • Contribute to the enhancement of forecasting methodologies, models, controls, and reporting processes to improve efficiency, transparency, and decision-making.

  • Respond to ad hoc analyses, business requests, and strategic initiatives with timely, accurate, and well-supported recommendations.

  • Foster strong working relationships across functional teams and serve as a trusted partner in balancing strategic objectives, financial performance, and risk considerations.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

  • 3-5+ years of experience in financial services, with Treasury, ALM, balance sheet management, forecasting, or related experience preferred.

  • Experience with QRM or similar asset liability management and forecasting platforms required.

  • Demonstrated ability to analyze complex financial information, solve problems, and drive process improvements.

  • Strong understanding of banking products, financial markets, and the regulatory environment affecting balance sheet management.

  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; experience with data analytics and automation tools is preferred.

  • Strong quantitative, analytical, and critical thinking skills.

  • Proven ability to communicate complex concepts effectively to diverse audiences, including senior management.

  • Demonstrated success building collaborative relationships across functions and influencing stakeholders in a matrixed environment.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality results in a fast-paced environment.

jobTitle: Head of Technology Process Re-Engineering, Managing Director
jobDescription:
Who we are looking for

We are seeking a Managing Director level Head of Technology Process Re-Engineering to establish and lead a GTS-focused capability for technology process mapping, process re-engineering, and operational transparency across State Street Global Technology Services. This role will report to the GTS Head of Process Improvement and Risk Remediation. This role will drive the development of standardized process views for key GTS technology processes, improve end-to-end process understanding, and identify opportunities to simplify, optimize, and strengthen control effectiveness within the GTS operating environment.

The ideal candidate is a senior technology transformation leader with deep experience in process mapping, operating model design, and process re-engineering within a large, complex, and regulated technology organization. This individual must be able to translate fragmented knowledge into clear, actionable process maps and improvement roadmaps that support GTS decision-making, risk reduction, and sustained operational improvement.

This is a GTS-facing leadership role expected to partner with GTS senior leaders, technology process owners, risk partners, platform teams, and global delivery organizations. The Head of Technology Process Mapping will be expected to define the standards, tooling approach, and governance model for GTS process mapping while also leading hands-on efforts to document, analyze, redesign, and embed improved ways of working.

What you will be responsible for

GTS Technology Process Mapping Strategy & Execution

  • Define and lead the GTS technology process mapping approach, including standards, methodology, taxonomy, tooling approach, and adoption model for documenting critical technology processes across GTS functions.
  • Build and maintain clear end-to-end views of priority GTS processes, connecting activities, roles, systems, handoffs, controls, pain points, and performance indicators to improve transparency and accountability.
  • Build out and lead a small team of process mapping professionals across two global locations, ensuring consistent standards, delivery quality, and stakeholder engagement across the GTS process mapping portfolio.

Process Re-engineering, Optimization & Control Improvement

  • Lead structured process analysis to identify duplication, fragmentation, manual workarounds, unclear ownership, control gaps, and opportunities to simplify or standardize execution.
  • Partner with GTS process owners and transformation teams to design future-state processes, clarify roles and decision rights, and develop practical implementation roadmaps that improve efficiency, risk management, and operating discipline.
  • Establish measurable outcomes for GTS process re-engineering efforts, including reduced complexity, improved cycle times, stronger control alignment, clearer accountability, and better management reporting.

Governance, Standards & Executive Reporting

  • Create and maintain governance routines that ensure GTS technology process maps remain current, validated, owned, and aligned to GTS standards, control expectations, and management reporting needs.
  • Develop executive-ready reporting that communicates GTS process coverage, mapping maturity, key risks, improvement opportunities, open decisions, and progress against technology process improvement priorities.

Stakeholder Leadership & Change Adoption

  • Lead engagement with senior stakeholders across GTS technology, risk, operations, and delivery teams to drive alignment on current-state understanding, future-state design, prioritization of improvement opportunities, and adoption of redesigned processes.
  • Build credibility with global teams by facilitating fact-based discussions, resolving ownership ambiguity, challenging legacy ways of working, and helping teams move from process documentation to measurable process improvement.

What we value

  • Technology Process Leadership: Proven ability to define and scale process mapping, process architecture, and process re-engineering capabilities within a large, matrixed technology organization.
  • Re-engineering Mindset: Demonstrated experience identifying process inefficiencies and translating analysis into practical redesign options, implementation plans, and measurable outcomes.
  • Executive Stakeholder Influence: Ability to engage senior leaders, challenge constructively, build consensus, and drive decisions across organizational boundaries.
  • Risk and Control Orientation: Strong understanding of how process design, ownership, controls, metrics, and evidence support operational resilience and a sound control environment.
  • Structured Communication: Exceptional written, verbal, and facilitation skills, with the ability to convert complex processes into clear narratives, visual maps, decision materials, and executive-ready recommendations.
  • Analytical Depth: Strong ability to evaluate process data, control evidence, performance indicators, organizational handoffs, and operating model constraints to identify root causes and improvement opportunities.
  • Change Leadership: Ability to move GTS teams from documentation to adoption by embedding standards, reinforcing accountability, and sustaining improved ways of working across global technology teams.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

  • 15+ years of experience leading technology process transformation, process re-engineering, business architecture, operational excellence, technology transformation, or risk-aligned remediation initiatives within large organizations.
  • Experience operating at a senior leadership level, preferably within financial services, technology, operations, risk management, or another highly regulated environment.
  • Demonstrated expertise with process mapping and re-engineering methods such as BPMN, SIPOC, value stream mapping, Lean, Six Sigma, business capability mapping, operating model design, or related disciplines.
  • Experience building process standards, governance models, repositories, reusable templates, maturity assessments, and executive reporting for technology process improvement programs.
  • Strong track record working with globally distributed technology teams and influencing senior stakeholders across GTS, risk, operations, and business-aligned technology functions.

We are seeking a senior testing leader to partner closely with Implementation Test Leads and delivery stakeholders to manage all aspects of test execution for Alpha implementations. This role is accountable for end-to-end testing governance, execution oversight, and cross-functional coordination to ensure high-quality, predictable, and scalable delivery outcomes across complex client implementations. These programs span complex business models and data flows across front, middle, and back-office operations involving State Street, Charles River Development, clients, and industry partners. 

 

Why this role is important to us 

Alpha is State Street’s front-to-back platform integrating front, middle, and back-office capabilities. Successful Alpha implementations depend on disciplined, execution-focused testing that is tightly aligned with program delivery, performance readiness, and adoption of automation. This role ensures testing is executed as a core delivery function, not a standalone activity, enabling accelerated timelines, reduced risk, and superior client outcomes. 

 

What you will be responsible for 

  • Partner with Implementation Test Leads to manage end-to-end test execution for assigned Alpha implementations, ensuring alignment with overall program milestones and delivery objectives.  

  • Own and govern all aspects of testing execution, including:  

  • Test strategy and approach 

  • Detailed test planning and scheduling 

  • Execution management across test phases 

  • Defect management, triage, and resolution governance 

  • Status reporting, risk management, and executive communications 

  • Provide strong project management oversight for testing workstreams, including dependency management, issue escalation, and change control.  

  • Act as the primary testing execution interface with Implementation Leads, PMO, business stakeholders, and technology partners.  

  • Partner closely with the System Performance team to ensure performance testing is planned, executed, and integrated into overall test cycles.  

  • Partner with the Automation team to drive adoption and execution of automation strategies, ensuring optimal coverage, reusability, and alignment with implementation timelines.  

  • Ensure consistent application of testing standards, governance, and best practices across implementations.  

  • Oversee execution across global, multi-vendor and multi-location teams, ensuring clear accountability and delivery discipline.  

  • Provide transparent, data-driven test reporting to senior leadership, highlighting progress, risks, and mitigation actions.  

  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of the Alpha testing delivery model, including execution frameworks, metrics, and tooling.  

  • Support client engagements by setting clear testing expectations, execution plans, and success criteria. 

 

 

 

What we value

jobTitle: Alpha Implementations Defect Test Manager, Vice President
jobDescription:
Who we are looking for

We are seeking an experienced Defect Test Manager to lead defect governance across complex Alpha implementations. Working closely with Implementation Test Leads, programme leadership, business and technology teams, clients and third-party providers, the role is accountable for the complete defect lifecycle, from identification and validation through prioritisation, remediation, retesting and closure. The successful candidate will be proactive in establishing a disciplined, transparent and data-driven approach to defect management across front, middle and back-office processes, integrations and data flows.

Why this role is important to us

Alpha is State Street’s integrated front-to-back platform. Effective defect management is critical to protecting delivery milestones, solution quality, operational readiness and client confidence. This role provides clear accountability for defect governance, ensuring issues are accurately assessed, prioritised according to risk, resolved within agreed timeframes and supported by robust evidence for test completion and go-live decisions.

What you will be responsible for

  • Own and continuously enhance the defect management framework, operating model and governance standards across all Alpha testing activities and client implementations.
  • Manage the end-to-end defect lifecycle across all test phases, including identification, validation, classification, prioritisation, assignment, remediation, retesting, closure and retention of audit evidence.
  • Define and enforce defect severity, priority, ownership, service-level expectations and closure criteria.
  • Chair defect triage and review forums, ensuring consistent decisions based on business and client impact, technical risk, test coverage and delivery milestones.
  • Maintain a controlled defect backlog, with clear ownership, target resolution dates, dependencies, ageing and escalation paths.
  • Provide objective defect metrics, trend analysis and quality insights for programme governance, status reporting and executive decision-making.
  • Ensure material defects, accepted risks, workarounds and deferred items are formally assessed, approved and traceable.
  • Coordinate business, testing, product, development, infrastructure, data and vendor teams to remove impediments and accelerate resolution of priority defects.
  • Challenge incomplete or insufficient defect records and ensure that supporting evidence, reproducible steps, impact assessments and diagnostic information are provided.
  • Monitor defect leakage, rejection, duplication, reopen rates, ageing and resolution performance, identifying systemic quality concerns and corrective actions.
  • Lead escalations for critical and high-priority defects, ensuring that business impact, recovery plans and management decisions are clearly documented.
  • Assess defect readiness against test exit and go-live criteria, providing a clear view of residual risk and recommendations to programme leadership.
  • Partner with Test Leads to plan retesting and regression coverage, confirm resolution evidence and prevent premature closure.
  • Maintain effective controls within defect management tools, including workflows, mandatory fields, status transitions, dashboards and management reporting.
  • Oversee defect management across global, multi-vendor and multi-location teams, establishing clear accountability and consistent working practices.
  • Facilitate root-cause analysis for recurring or material defects and track preventive actions through to completion.
  • Drive continuous improvement in defect governance, reporting, controls and stakeholder engagement by applying delivery insights and lessons learned.

What we value

  • Strong leadership presence and the judgement to influence senior business, technology, programme and client stakeholders.
  • Strong stakeholder management, with the confidence to escalate issues constructively, navigate challenging stakeholder relationships and maintain focus until defects are fully and effectively resolved.
  • Proven experience leading defect management across large-scale financial services or technology transformation programmes.
  • Sound judgement in balancing delivery urgency, solution quality, client impact and operational risk.
  • Excellent facilitation, negotiation, escalation and executive reporting skills.
  • Strong understanding of front, middle and back-office workflows, data movement, interfaces and integration risks.
  • A disciplined, evidence-based approach to governance, control and continuous improvement.

Skills and experience required

  • End-to-end defect lifecycle management and governance
  • Defect triage leadership, severity and priority assessment, and risk-based decision-making
  • Advanced defect reporting, trend analysis, ageing analysis and executive dashboards
  • Root-cause analysis, corrective-action tracking and quality improvement
  • Advanced knowledge of Jira, with the ability to configure and apply defect workflows, maintain detailed defect records, and produce consolidated reporting and trend analysis across multiple client implementations.
  • Leadership of globally distributed teams, suppliers and cross-functional stakeholders
  • Clear, concise and evidence-based communication at programme and executive governance forums

Education and preferred qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience in technology, finance, management or a related discipline
  • Substantial experience in software testing, quality assurance or implementation delivery within financial services or complex technology environments
  • Demonstrable experience owning defect governance across multiple test phases and integrated delivery teams
  • Relevant testing, quality management or project delivery certification is advantageous

This role is critical in ensuring the integrity, accuracy, and availability of data used across investment, risk, compliance, and client reporting functions. The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of financial instruments, data governance, and data quality frameworks, with hands-on experience in SQL and programming languages to support data mapping, transformation, and analysis.
The role is accountable for ensuring that ADS commitments are clearly documented and managed and for managing the risk of delays slippage and communications out to the wider team.


The successful candidate will work within a data operations and governance model, supporting both BAU processes and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance data quality, reduce exceptions, and strengthen platform reliability. Job Description:

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) awarded the Technical Support Services Contract 5 (T5) to Parsons in April 2023. Parsons is the prime contractor. This $1.8+ billion contract has a 4-year base period with two 3-year options. The statement of work includes a variety of activities that support the FAA’s Capital Investment Plan (CIP) and certain reimbursable programs, the FAA NextGen Program, national security programs and aviation safety. Specifically, work includes site selection and engineering, construction, environmental and fire/life safety, equipment installation and testing, drafting, contract surveillance, and other technical services as required. Work is performed across the nation in each of the FAA’s nine regions as well as the Aeronautical Center in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, and the Technical Center in Atlantic City, New Jersey and in several U.S. territories. An average staff of 500 with a peak staff over 650 supports this contract, in addition to those subcontractors who perform construction work.


The SCA – Engineering Technician serves as an experienced field technician supporting the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) under the TSSC-5 contract. This position performs installation, modification, testing, troubleshooting, repair, and preventive maintenance on a variety of electronic systems and equipment that support the National Airspace System (NAS).

The Engineering Technician works under limited supervision, following established procedures, technical documentation, and FAA directives. The technician may work independently on routine or moderately complex tasks and supports senior technicians or engineers on more complex systems and activities.

Perform installation, relocation, and removal of electronic systems and equipment, which may include:

  • Navigation aids (NAVAIDS)

  • Communications systems (VHF/UHF, data/voice)

  • Surveillance and support systems

  • Associated power, grounding, and control equipment

Troubleshoot and repair systems to the unit, board, or module level as assigned:

  • Use standard test equipment (digital multimeters, signal generators, oscilloscopes, etc.)

  • Follow step-by-step troubleshooting guides, fault isolation procedures, and technical manuals

  • Escalate complex or recurring issues to crew lead, FAA counterparts, and project management.

Read and work from:

  • Schematics, wiring diagrams, and interconnect drawings

  • Equipment manuals, technical orders, and job plans

  • FAA orders, work instructions, and site-specific procedures

Assist in field installations and site work under TSSC‑5:

  • Support pre-installation checks and site preparation

  • Install racks, cabinets, and equipment per drawings and installation standards

  • Route, terminate, label, and test cables (coax, fiber, copper) under guidance

  • Assist with system power-up, basic alignment, and functional testing

Use and care for test and measurement equipment:

  • Configure and operate standard electronic test instruments

  • Perform basic measurements, alignments, and performance checks

  • Maintain proper calibration and handle equipment in accordance with procedure

Document work activities in accordance with contract and FAA requirements:

  • Complete maintenance logs, service tickets, and test forms

  • Record parts used, corrective actions taken, and test results

  • Provide redline/as-built information to senior technicians or engineers

Follow all safety, security, and quality practices:

  • Comply with FAA and Parsons safety policies, OSHA regulations, and site Risk Management Plans

  • Adhere to physical and information security requirements at FAA facilities

  • Follow configuration control and quality assurance procedures

  • Collaborate effectively with senior technicians, engineers, project managers, and FAA representatives to support project objectives.

What Required Skills You'll Bring:

  • High school diploma is required.

  • May require repetitive movement such as lifting up to 50 lbs., bending, and standing.

  • Basic Microsoft suite and Internet, and E-mail.

  • Must be able to meet customer security requirements. A background check by federal authorities will be performed.

  • Must be able to travel up to 100% within the USA.

  • Five plus years of working knowledge of:

    • Basic analog and digital electronics

    • Fundamentals of RF and communications equipment

    • Use of standard electronic test equipment (DMMs, basic scopes, signal generators)

  • Ability to:

    • Read and interpret basic schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical documentation

    • Follow written and verbal instructions and standard procedures

    • Work safely in field, shop, and facility environment

Security Clearance Requirement:

None

Job Description:

T5 PROJECT MANAGER REQUISITION 

Ready to put your project management expertise to work on complex projects? Are you great with people and have a track record managing teams that get the job done? Parsons is now hiring an experienced Project Manager with a desire to work on creating innovative, practical solutions to various projects in support of Federal Aviation Administration’s Technical Support Services Contract (TSSC). 

In this role you will be responsible for all aspects of project management for multiple concurrent projects at various geographic locations. Responsibilities include leading project teams; planning, design, execution, and closeout of assigned projects to meet client objectives and in accordance with contract terms and corporate policies; and engagement with various client POCs to meet their expectations and earn new work. 

Parsons extensive experience in this field, combined with your experience coordinating projects through all phases of the job will propel your career and leadership opportunities forward. We need our Project Managers to be versatile, enthusiastic, team-oriented, and have exceptional communication, analytical and organizational skills  

Under the $1.8B+ Technical Support Services Contract 5 (T5) awarded in April 2023, Parsons serves as the prime contractor supporting the FAA’s Capital Investment Plan (CIP) modernization. This contract includes a four-year base period with two three-year options. Parsons delivers site selection and engineering, construction, environmental and fire/life safety, equipment installation and testing, drafting, and specialized technical services. Work is performed across the Central Service Area 

POSITION OVERVIEW 

The Project Manager will be responsible for cradle-to-grave management of various FAA infrastructure projects. Project Management tasks will include writing work plans, estimating construction costs and reporting project status throughout its lifecycle. The Project Manager will be the direct link between the regional customer and the project execution team. The Project Manager will report directly to the Regional Program Manager. Duties will also include establishing milestones; monitoring and adhering to schedules; identification of issues; and implementing solutions, such as allocation of resources or changing contractual specifications. The Project Manager will direct the work of employees assigned to the program/project  including technical, engineering, construction and administrative areas and may provide technical guidance to less-experienced field engineering personnel. The Project Manager also serves as primary customer contact for program activities, leading program review sessions with the customer to discuss cost, schedule, and technical performance. 

Under general supervision, the Project Manager participates in the development, execution, supervision, and coordination of all technical aspects of field engineering assignments. The Project Manager is also responsible for reviewing the performance of subcontractors to assure contract compliance, the application of accepted construction technology and standards, and the acceptable standardization of materials and supplies.  

RESPONSIBILITIES 

 

  • Leads interdisciplinary teams of project professionals and manages their work effort. 

  • Prepares work plans based on customer scope of work packages to include project execution approach, risk management, project schedule, and project budget.  

  • Develops risk management plan for each assigned project in collaboration with the Risk Specialist to identify and control hazards associated with the work activities.  

  • Ensures assigned personnel engage in safe work practices in compliance with site-specific safety procedures and industry standards. 

  • Makes decisions regarding long-range planning, scheduling, budgeting, work priorities, and personnel.  

  • Ensures project deliverables meet contractual requirements and customer expectations.   

  • Provides advice on field engineering procedures, construction methods, and financial matters to management. 

  • Negotiates changes to the scope of work with the client and key subcontractors in coordination with the Procurement Team.  

  • Manages subcontractor activities through the subcontract administrators to develop RFPs, review bids, and ensures subcontractor compliance with project and subcontract requirements. 

  • Maintains project control documentation, design drawings and specifications, and project revisions. 

  • Develops and executes actions to mitigate potential cost overruns or delays, or to accommodate significant changes to the scope of work. Advises the client and company management of any such changes.  

  • Promotes technical and commercial excellence on the project by ensuring quality processes are implemented. 

  • Monitors and reports to management on the progress of all project activity within the program, including significant milestones, and any conditions, which would affect project cost, schedule, or quality.  

  • Establishes weekly meetings to review project status and formulate action items.  

 

 

SKILLS/COMPETENCIES 

 

Requires comprehensive knowledge of engineering and construction-related processes as well as industry practices and demonstrated experience engaging with customers and managing subcontractors.  Also requires excellent written and oral communication skills, and familiarity with AutoCAD and other PC software packages typically associated with engineering and construction and performing in a lead capacity on a project.   

 

Experience and familiarity with FAA  federal and local coordination and project requirements is desired. Proven ability to perform in a management capacity. 

 

QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Bachelor's Degree in a technical or construction-related field (or equivalent experience accepted)

  • 10+ years of related work experience on large scale programs. 

  • 3+ years in a leadership role at a field site

  • Project Management Certification (PMP) preferred. 

 

OTHER REQUIREMENTS 

  • Up to 15% - 20% travel may be required to effectively manage assigned projects. 

  • Must be able to meet customer security requirements. A background check by Federal Authorities will be performed.  

 

Security Clearance Requirement:

None
