jobTitle: Principal Associate – Events Project Manager, Community Finance, Impact & Investment
jobDescription:
Principal Associate – Events Project Manager, Community Finance, Impact & Investment

Capital One, a Fortune 500 company and one of the nation’s top 10 banks, offers a broad spectrum of financial products and services to consumers, small businesses and commercial clients. Our mission is to create one of the nation’s great banks, and we have the necessary ingredients: a strong balance sheet, resilient businesses, a massive customer franchise, strong analytical capabilities, and great people. We nurture a work environment where people with a variety of thoughts, ideas and backgrounds, guided by our shared Values, come together to make Capital One a great company – and a great place to work.

Global Enterprise Affairs (GEA) works to change banking for good through the collective efforts of seven teams and key partnerships across the enterprise. We engage internal and external stakeholders to help build a more inclusive society, strengthen communities, and create financial tools that enrich lives. Our teams include Global Enterprise Communications, Community Finance, Impact and Investment (CFI&I), CRA Strategy and Program Management, the Global Policy Affairs Group (GPAG), Regulatory Relations, and Strategy & Enablement.  Through our teams, we have unparalleled access to a diverse group of motivated changemakers similarly focused on the ingredients for a more perfect future.

The Opportunity and Role:

CFI&I is driving a multi-year transformation to increasingly align business strategy with profound social and economic impact. By uniting the distinct strengths of our Community Finance team (specializing in affordable housing, CDFI loans, and complex capital investments) and our Community Impact & Investment team (focused on enterprise volunteerism, market research, grantmaking, and LOB advisory), CFI&I deploys a holistic, data-driven approach to community advancement and financial inclusion.

We are seeking a Principal Associate, Project Manager - CFI&I Strategic Events & Convenings to join our team. 

This is a role for an intentional, rigorous project manager and experienced events producer who seamlessly balances meticulous detail with the broader strategic picture. You will be responsible for the end-to-end planning, execution, and delivery of multiple high-stakes engagements and large-scale strategic events simultaneously. These convenings provide best-in-class experiences for senior executives and key external stakeholders, building Capital One’s reputation in the external environment while advancing critical business priorities. The ideal candidate will bring a background in project management, Customer Experience (CX), and/or large-scale event planning, alongside the unique ability to build consensus quickly and actively shape and influence intent and strategy across highly matrixed teams.

In this role, you’ll be expected to demonstrate proficiency in these primary responsibilities:

  • Lead full-lifecycle planning, intent design, logistics, site selection, venue management, and execution of CFI&I's strategic events, summit convenings, and executive roundtables.

  • Oversee detailed event budgets, cost forecasting, vendor contract negotiations (AV, catering, venues, production agencies), and procurement processes to maximize ROI and operational efficiency.

  • Oversee live on-site execution and partnership with vendors. 

  • Shape and influence event intent and strategy by translating complex enterprise and local team goals into actionable, premium event concepts.

  • Build consensus quickly across a matrixed environment, partnering closely with CF and CI&I leaders, internal corporate teams, senior executives, vendors, and external partners.

  • Deliver a best-in-class customer experience by integrating hospitality best practices, seamless guest journeys, and premium touchpoints into every convening when appropriate.

  • Create repeatable frameworks, templates, and playbooks to scale and mature the centralized events management function.

  • Provide real-time strategic counsel and status updates to stakeholders and senior leaders to navigate evolving business needs.

  • Orchestrate cross-functional collaboration between Community Finance, Community Impact & Investment, GPAG, GEC, LOBs, and external partners.

  • Measure and report on event impact by tracking KPIs and producing high-quality, executive-ready decks and briefings.

  • Work seamlessly as part of a collaborative team, proactively rolling up your sleeves to solve complex problems and automate workflows.
     

We want you if you are: 

  • Impact-Driven. You dream big. You desire to make the world a better place, and you get energy from working with others with similar passions to accomplish big, bold goals.

  • Mission-Forward. Passion for community development, affordable housing, and social impact within commercial finance.

  • Wired for Collaboration and Connection. You thrive in a matrixed organization because you know that together we can do better. You’re obsessed with building and cultivating relationships. You have a proven track record of building solutions co-delivered across teams 

  • Customer Focused. You care about doing what’s best for the community and for Capital One associates. You don’t shy away from hard conversations or nuanced decision making because you know the best outcomes often go hand in hand with tough decisions. For the sake of the associate experience, you are comfortable holding your partners and your own team accountable for results.

  • Process Oriented. You loathe inefficient processes and look for ways to streamline and document everything you touch. You enjoy creating new processes when it is needed. 

  • Enablement is your middle name. You are passionate about building tools that enable others, because you get energized by seeing those around you enabled to do their best work.

  • Do-er. You’re biased toward action, you try things and sometimes you fail. You can get around your own roadblocks and you remove obstacles for your team to stay focused on enterprise goals.

Basic Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma, GED or equivalent certification

  • At least 4 years of experience in project management, process management, project delivery, or any combination of the three

  • At least 4 years of experience in event management, logistics, project management, or any combination of the three

  • At least 2 years of experience managing third-party partner relationships and budget forecasting

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree or Military Experience

  • At least 6 years of experience driving large-scale corporate events, executive summits, or multi-stakeholder strategic convenings

  • At least 3 years of experience directly advising and presenting to senior executive stakeholders (VP level and above)

  • At least 3 years of experience leading cross-functional teams and managing complex, highly matrixed stakeholder environments 

  • Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified Meeting Professional (CMP), Lean, Agile, or Six Sigma certification

  • Experience designing repeatable frameworks, operational playbooks, and standardized tools to scale organizational capabilities 

  • Experience in financial services, community impact, and/or affordable housing industry

jobTitle: Senior Associate, Data Scientist - Beyond AML Modeling & Innovations
jobDescription:
Senior Associate, Data Scientist - Beyond AML Modeling & Innovations

Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

Team Description

The Beyond AML Modeling & Innovations (BAMI) team within the Enterprise Risk Organization leverages AI to modernize and transform how we assess risk. We are a small but mighty team of data scientists and business analysts who partner closely with stakeholders to design and deploy innovative solutions. In this role, you will have the opportunity to drive a variety of 0-to-1 projects, utilizing traditional machine learning, natural language processing, graph-based modeling, and Generative AI and more to solve novel, complex challenges. You will have the opportunity to leverage your creativity and business sense in combination with technical skills to build holistic solutions that can address the heart of our stakeholder’s pain points.

Role Description

In this role, you will:

  • Partner with a cross-functional team of data scientists, software engineers, and product managers to deliver a product customers love

  • Leverage a broad stack of technologies — Python, Conda, AWS, H2O, Spark, and more — to reveal the insights hidden within huge volumes of numeric and textual data

  • Build machine learning models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, validation, and implementation

  • Flex your interpersonal skills to translate the complexity of your work into tangible business goals

The Ideal Candidate is:

  • Innovative. You continually research and evaluate emerging technologies. You stay current on published state-of-the-art methods, technologies, and applications and seek out opportunities to apply them.

  • Creative. You thrive on bringing definition to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and pushing hard to find answers. You’re not afraid to share a new idea.

  • Technical. You’re comfortable with open-source languages and are passionate about developing further. You have hands-on experience developing data science solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms.

  • Statistically-minded. You’ve built models, validated them, and backtested them. You know how to interpret a confusion matrix or a ROC curve. You have experience with clustering, classification, sentiment analysis, time series, and deep learning.

  • A data guru. “Big data” doesn’t faze you. You have the skills to retrieve, combine, and analyze data from a variety of sources and structures. You know understanding the data is often the key to great data science.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining one of the following with an expectation that the required degree will be obtained on or before the scheduled start date:

    • A Bachelor's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) plus 2 years of experience performing data analytics

    • A Master's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) or an MBA with a quantitative concentration

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s Degree in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics), or PhD in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics)

  • Experience working with AWS

  • At least 2 years’ experience in Python, Scala, or R

  • At least 2 years’ experience with machine learning

  • At least 2 years’ experience with SQL

Machine Learning Engineer 5 (IC)

Do you love building and pioneering in the AI and technology space? Do you enjoy solving complex business problems in a fast-paced, collaborative, inclusive, and iterative delivery environment? At Capital One, you'll be part of a big group of makers, breakers, doers and disruptors who love to solve real problems and meet real customer needs. We are seeking Machine Learning Engineers who are passionate about leveraging cutting-edge open source frameworks, advanced algorithms, and emerging technologies to join our team. As a Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll have the opportunity to be on the forefront of driving major AI transformations and scaling production models across Capital One.


What You’ll Do:

  • The MLE role overlaps with many disciplines, such as Ops, Modeling, and Data Engineering. In this role, you'll be expected to perform many ML engineering activities, including one or more of the following:
  • Design, build, and/or deliver ML models and components that solve real-world business problems, while working in collaboration with the Product and Data Science teams
  • Build and scale massive multi-tenant platforms that enable running large footprint ML model training and/or serving at scale
  • Inform your ML infrastructure decisions using your understanding of ML modeling techniques and issues, including choice of model, data, and feature selection, model training, hyperparameter tuning, dimensionality, bias/variance, and validation)
  • Solve complex problems by writing and testing application code, developing and validating ML models, and automating tests and deployment
  • Collaborate as part of a cross-functional Agile team to create and enhance software that enables state-of-the-art big data and ML applications
  • Retrain, maintain, and monitor models in production
  • Leverage or build cloud-based architectures, technologies, and/or platforms to deliver optimized ML models at scale.
  • Construct optimized data pipelines to feed ML models
  • Leverage continuous integration and continuous deployment best practices, including test automation and monitoring, to ensure successful deployment of ML models and application code
  • Ensure all code is well-managed to reduce vulnerabilities, models are well-governed from a risk perspective, and the ML follows best practices in Responsible and Explainable AI
  • Use programming languages like Python, Scala, or Java

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree or higher in Computer Science, Machine Learning or a related quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Engineering)
  • At least 6 years of experience programming with Python, Java, Golang, or C++
  • At least 6 years of Machine Learning experience using industry standard frameworks PyTorch or Tensorflow and libraries (Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn)
  • At least 6 years of experience using and operating large scale distributed systems (Spark, Ray) to prepare AI/ML data
  • At least 4 years of experience deploying and operating Machine Learning solutions in production and operating production services in the cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure) and using Kubernetes to manage large scale containerized ML software systems

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's or Doctoral Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, or related field
  • 5+ years of experience optimizing ML algorithms, configurations, and infrastructure
  • 5+ years of experience following software development best practices including source control, testing, code reviews, CI/CD, etc. 
  • 5+ years of experience building resilient software solutions with pre-production testing, advanced deployment techniques (one-box, blue/green, gradual dial-up), monitoring, alarms, and preparing incident response plans
  • 5+ years of experience working with Machine Learning techniques (Supervised, semi-supervised, and unsupervised, reinforcement learning, etc.) model types (Regression, Classification, Clustering, etc.), model Architectures (RNNs, CNNs, LSTMs, Transformers), training concepts (loss function, hyperparameters, regularization), and how to evaluate model accuracy and diagnose and address common issues (underfitting, overfitting)
  • 5+ years of experience designing, implementing, and scaling production-ready data pipelines for training and evaluating ML models
  • ML industry impact through conference presentations, papers, blog posts, open source contributions, or patents
  • Ability to communicate complex technical and machine learning concepts clearly to a variety of audiences

Role Expectations 

As a Product Designer, you’ll combine your craft expertise and leadership skills with an understanding of our customers and the business to co-create innovative solutions to complex problems and influence product strategy.

Here are some of the expected competencies for this role:

Product Design Expertise: Demonstrate a high degree of skill in product design, leveraging a variety of skills across interaction, visual and service design; in collaboration with cross-functional partners, inform the use of appropriate tools, platforms, frameworks and design systems and creates artifacts that may include journey maps, blueprints, high-fidelity designs and prototypes

Leadership: Lead design projects, directing and delegating work for more junior team members and building strong partnerships with cross-functional stakeholders while also mentoring and helping to mature the overall product design practice at Capital One

Human-Centered: Effectively navigate the needs of partners and stakeholders, leveraging critical-thinking skills that factor in data, research insights, scalability and tech constraints, while ensuring the team focuses on customer-centered solutions and inclusive design

Collaboration: Leverage a rich network of partnerships across lines of business and the organization to foster collaboration and share solutions, incorporating cross-functional perspectives to bridge gaps in information and drive product strategy

The ideal candidate has a strong portfolio demonstrating your leadership, process, results and impact.

Full Time Branch Ambassador - Railroad

Welcome to the future of banking. At Capital One, we believe your bank should be as mobile, intuitive, and human as the rest of your life. We are reimagining the way people interact with their money by creating community hubs where technology meets human empathy.


As a Branch Ambassador, you are the heartbeat of our space. You don't just "process transactions"—you embody our culture of outstanding hospitality. You are a relationship-builder who blends friendly, attentive service with cutting-edge digital innovation. Whether you’re helping a client navigate our latest tools or empowering them to reach their financial goals, you are the face of an exceptional, human-centric experience.

We are looking for curious, empathetic, and tech-savvy individuals who thrive in a fast-moving environment. You are someone who doesn't wait to be asked; you anticipate needs, solve problems before they arise, and have a genuine passion for helping people thrive in an evolving digital world.


What You’ll Actually Do

The Guardian of Trust & Accuracy You are the bedrock of our environment’s safety and integrity. You’ll execute high-volume cash transactions—including deposits, withdrawals, and complex negotiable instrument processing—with 100% accuracy. You maintain a "compliance-first" mindset, ensuring all security, audit, BSA/AML, and federal regulatory standards are met with precision to keep our customers' assets safe.

The Digital Concierge You are a mentor in a digital world. You’ll educate clients on how to leverage mobile banking, remote deposit capture, and contactless payments, helping them gain convenience and security in their daily financial lives.

The First-Line Consultant You aren’t just answering questions; you’re identifying needs. By actively listening, you’ll uncover personal or business goals and pair them with the right digital tools or banking solutions to help them succeed.

The Hospitality Lead You move fluidly throughout the space, greeting customers and ensuring no one ever feels like just a "number." You balance the efficiency of a high-volume operation with the warmth of a community-focused partner.


What You Bring

  • A Hospitality Heart: You have a natural gift for making people feel welcome and heard.
  • Tech Fluency: You are an early adopter of apps and digital tools and love teaching others how to use them.
  • Precision and Detail: You find satisfaction in getting the numbers right every single time and following clear procedures.
  • Adaptability: You enjoy a "fluid" workspace where you might move from a cash drawer to a digital demo in minutes.
  • Curiosity: You want to know the "why" behind the "how" and are always looking for ways to improve the customer journey.

Why Join Us?

This isn't just a job—it’s work with a mission. Because we’ve removed the pressure of traditional sales quotas, you are free to focus on the depth of your impact on customers, teammates, and the community. We provide an inclusive environment where we invest in your confidence, service mindset, and professional growth. We ensure you have the tools to be stronger in your role and more effective in how you show up every day.


The Perks

We provide a comprehensive benefits package designed to fuel your journey. Whether you’re using our education assistance to prepare for your next career move, or taking advantage of our mental and physical health resources to stay at your best, we invest in you as a whole person. Our goal is to ensure that wherever your career takes you—within Capital One or into the wider world—you leave the Branch stronger than when you started.

  • Experience working in an agile development environment and collaborating across technical and business teams.
  • Experience with version control systems such as Git.
  • Experience working with People data, including workforce and Talent Acquisition data, and familiarity with People analytics platforms such as Visier.

We’re looking for a Reliability and Failure Analysis Engineer to join our team! You’ll be responsible for developing and executing reliability programs for developing and qualifying our display technologies, as well as leading failure analysis. The display technologies are used in the next generation of Specs wearable computing devices such as Spectacles.

What you’ll do: 

  • Work with the wider operations team, engineering (EE, ME and NPI), designers, and contract manufacturers to plan and execute reliability testing to assess product durability and corrective action effectiveness, complete failure analysis, and implement corrective action  
  • Determine, develop, demonstrate and systematize methods of assessment for components, subassemblies and process required to ensure each meet quality and reliability requirements
  • Provide subject matter expertise on reliability test methodology, measurement of device integrity, and test to failure approaches to understand design margin
  • Implement data collection, storage and data reduction for the purposes of providing real time accessible data and communication of ongoing testing activities
  • Support new technology developments: materials, processes, components and subassemblies using a systemic approach for risk prioritization and reliability growth.
  • Support prototype builds with contract manufacturers
  • Technology and strategy development
  • Identify high risk failure modes early in the design life cycle and collaborate with other teams to evaluate and reduce risk.
  • Drive continuous improvement in FA capability and methods, reliability test, product reliability test outcomes and field Reliability for new products

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Demonstrated history working with EMS to prepare then execute reliability test plans and with engineering teams to communicate results, then analyze, correct and validate solutions to reliability test failures.
  • Demonstrated history completing and documenting failure analyses, inclusive of suggestions for corrective action and follow up validation testing
  • Experience personally operating and interpreting results of SEM/EDX, FTIR/DSC/TGA, CT X-ray, optical microscopy, OMM/CMM, Instron, potting/polishing cross-sections, and red-dye
  • Solid understanding of Six Sigma concepts and demonstrated capability to run Weibull and other model based reliability analyses 
  • Good understanding of the physics of failure and behind material properties (mechanical, electrical, and optical)
  • Able to prioritize duties and work well on your own
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with a high attention to detail
  • Excellent documentation and communication skills
  • Background working collaboratively with both internal and external partners, domestic and overseas

Minimum Qualifications:

  • B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Materials Science, chemistry, physics or equivalent
  • 7+ years of experience with FA, reliability testing and technology development

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Masters or higher level degree in Engineering or equivalent
  • Six Sigma Black Belt certification 
  • At least one previous role (>2years in duration) in consumer electronics industry

EHS Strategy & Leadership

  • Lead the development, governance, and continuous improvement of EHS standards, programs, and strategic initiatives across Specs Operations globally, ensuring consistency while enabling site specific operational requirements.

  • Own EHS programs supporting manufacturing, engineering, R&D, cleanroom, facilities, and operational functions.

Organizational Capability & Culture

  • Develop EHS competency frameworks, training strategies, and leadership engagement programs for employees, contractors, and leaders.

Program Management & Continuous Improvement

  • Establish EHS maturity assessments and continuous improvement roadmaps.
  • Manage EHS budgets, resource planning, and annual objectives.
  • Utilize data analytics, leading indicators, and risk trends to identify opportunities for operational improvement and risk reduction.
  • Develop business cases and strategic recommendations for EHS investments, staffing, and growth initiatives.

Incident Management & Emergency Preparedness

  • Lead investigations of serious incidents, significant near misses, and high potential events across assigned Specs locations.
  • Ensure robust root cause analysis methodologies are applied and corrective actions are effectively implemented and sustained.
  • Oversee emergency preparedness and EHS business continuity programs across assigned Specs locations, ensuring organizational readiness for operational disruptions, emergency events, and EHS business continuity risks.

  • Expert knowledge of EHS management systems, regulatory compliance, risk management, and strategic program development in manufacturing, R&D, cleanroom, semiconductor, advanced technology, or hardware development environments.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to communicate technical and regulatory risks to executive and non-technical audiences.

We’re looking for an experienced Health, Safety & Environmental (HSE) Advisor to support the HSE program at our Abingdon, UK facility.   • Work collaboratively with site and global HSE teams to share best practices and improve performance in Abingdon.

Compliance & Risk Management

  • Ensure compliance with UK environmental and occupational health and safety legislation, including the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, COSHH, DSEAR, PUWER, Environmental Permitting Regulations, and the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order.

  • Support the Management of Change (MOC) process for new equipment, process modifications, laboratory changes, and technology introductions.

  • Partner with engineering and operations teams to support safe installation, operation, and maintenance of toxic and hazardous gas systems, including gas cabinets, detection systems, and associated emergency controls in compliance with COSHH and DSEAR.

Hazardous Materials & manufacturing Safety

  • Manage site hazardous materials, hazardous waste, and toxic and hazardous gas safety programs, including governance, procedures, and engineering control strategies.

  • Ensure effective management of toxic and hazardous gas systems, including gas cabinets, detection and alarm systems, ventilation controls, and emergency response readiness, in compliance with COSHH and DSEAR.

  • Provide HSE leadership for manufacturing, laboratory, and cleanroom safety programs, including machine safety, laser safety, hazardous gases, and contractor safety.

  • Partner with engineering, facilities, and vendors to support safe design, installation, commissioning, and modification of tools and equipment.

Training, Culture & Engagement

  • Develop, coordinate, and deliver regulatory-required and role-based HSE training programs.

  • Champion a proactive safety culture through visible leadership, engagement with employees and contractors, and accountability at all levels.

  • Provide technical leadership to site safety committees and working groups, ensuring effective governance and follow-through on actions.

  • Apply modern safety principles, including Human and Organizational Performance (HOP), to strengthen system resilience and organizational learning.

Incident Management & Emergency Response

  • Lead investigations of incidents, near-misses, and high-potential events using root cause analysis and ensuring robust corrective and preventive actions.

  • Serve as the HSE lead for  emergency response activities during site events, coordinating with site leadership and post-incident recovery efforts as needed.

  • Ensure site emergency preparedness programs, emergency response teams, drills, and equipment readiness are established and maintained..

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Strong knowledge of UK HSE regulatory requirements and practical application in manufacturing, laboratory, or high-hazard environments.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead site-level HSE programs and influence cross-functional partners.

  • Strong risk assessment, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities in complex technical environments.

  • Ability to provide technical leadership, mentoring, or supervision to HSE professionals.

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage regulators, leadership, employees, and contractors.

  • Experience supporting the safe use and control of toxic and hazardous gases, including monitoring systems, emergency procedures, and compliance with DSEAR and COSHH requirements.

Minimum Qualifications: 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.

  • 5+ years of progressive experience in Environmental Health & Safety.

  • NEBOSH Diploma (Level 6) or equivalent professional qualification.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience leading HSE programs in semiconductor manufacturing, cleanroom, laboratory, or advanced manufacturing environments.

  • Experience implementing and sustaining  HSG65 principles, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 management systems.

Job Description

As an Advisor - Area Development, you will be responsible for meeting or exceeding revenue goals by managing, recruiting, and expanding volunteer and donor efforts throughout the area. You will also maximize funds raised for ALSAC, while increasing the support for and awareness of St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital.

Responsibilities

  • Establish and activate high-profile national fundraising initiatives throughout the area, including St. Jude Dream Home campaigns, radiothons, and other signature programs. Recruit volunteers, sponsors, and community partners to implement national program best practices, ensure campaign compliance, and maximize revenue.

  • Attain and exceed financial and stewardship goals, as established by territory and area leadership.

  • Use interpersonal and sales skills to create and build relationships with volunteers and donors through primarily face-to-face interaction, to recruit new partners and grow existing relationships.

  • Use fundraising knowledge to provide support, motivation, direction, and resources for fundraising initiatives to volunteers and donors through various communication channels, including personal visits, written correspondence, and electronic communication.

  • Create and implement marketing and recruitment plans for events through research and knowledge of current market trends and community engagement opportunities within the assigned area. Build and maintain relationships with media partners and support promotional activities that increase awareness and fundraising results.

  • Develop and grow multiple high-value ($250,000+) revenue-producing events (including dinners, galas, golf tournaments, dream homes and walks) with growth rates and expense ratios assigned by territory and area leadership.

  • Prepare written correspondence before and after events and maintain accurate records of all event contacts and revenues through appropriate tools and systems.

  • Serve as a public-facing representative of St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital by engaging with media partners, sponsors, volunteers, donors, and community stakeholders to strengthen relationships and increase brand awareness.

  • Work in collaboration with the internal area and enterprise team, volunteers and other stakeholders to identify, cultivate and solicit Dream Home and Radiothon donors. Conduct prospect research on potential donors and develop sponsorship proposals.

Qualifications

  • Five (5) years of relevant experience in fundraising, development, customer service, or sales.  Bachelor's degree is preferred.

  • Demonstrated relationship management success and proven experience and success in peer-to-peer fundraising.

  • Ability to relate to donors and volunteers from diverse backgrounds and cultures.

  • Strong communication, organizational, interpersonal, and public speaking skills.

  • Demonstrated project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholder relationships in a fast-paced environment.

  • Demonstrated negotiating and listening skills.

  • Donor/customer-oriented with excellent writing, telephone, and organizational skills.

  • Knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and fundraising software.

  • Demonstrates clear communication and the ability to influence others.

  • Ability to travel frequently within the Phoenix territory area by supporting events, volunteers, and partners in the assigned territory. Involves travel 15%-20%, including regular evening and weekend commitments during key campaign periods and fundraising events. Periodic visits to Memphis for enterprise, divisional, or donor events (on average 4-6 times annually) based on business needs.

  • Driver's License: A valid driver's license is required for this role.

This position is eligible for a hybrid schedule to include working from our Territory Office located at 645 East Missouri Avenue, Suite 255 Phoenix, AZ 85012.

Job Description

The Audit Manager is responsible for leading complex, high-impact internal audit engagements that add value and strengthen organizational operations. This role provides independent, objective assurance and advisory services by evaluating the effectiveness of internal controls, risk management, governance processes, financial reporting, and operational efficiency.

Reporting to the Chief Audit Officer, the Audit Manager operates with significant independence, exercising sound judgment and leadership while overseeing audit activities and mentoring audit staff.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead, manage, and deliver complex audit engagements from planning through reporting, ensuring quality, timeliness, and alignment with organizational priorities
  • Develop risk-based audit plans, including scope, objectives, methodologies, timelines, and resource allocation
  • Conduct and oversee risk assessments, process walkthroughs, and control evaluations to identify key risks and define audit strategies
  • Design and execute comprehensive audit programs and procedures aligned with audit objectives
  • Oversee audit fieldwork, including control testing, data analysis, and evaluation of financial and operational processes
  • Assess audit results, identify control deficiencies, and evaluate risk exposure
  • Develop practical, sustainable, and risk-based recommendations and effectively influence stakeholders to implement improvements
  • Prepare and review clear, concise, and well-supported audit reports and executive presentations for leadership and the Board Audit Committee
  • Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships across the organization; effectively manage conflict and drive alignment
  • Lead audit follow-up activities to ensure timely and effective remediation of audit findings
  • Provide guidance, coaching, and review of work performed by audit staff (if applicable)
  • Stay current on industry trends, regulatory changes, and best practices in internal auditing, risk management, and controls
  • Ensure all audit activities comply with the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) Standards for the Professional Practice of Internal Auditing
  • Communicate proactively with the Chief Audit Officer on audit progress, key risks, and emerging issues

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related field required. Master's degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of progressive internal audit experience, including leading complex audits and managing full audit lifecycles
  • Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) or equivalent (e.g., CPA, CISA, etc.) certification required, or ability to obtain certification within two years of hire
  • Demonstrated experience developing audit programs and driving audit execution independently
  • Strong knowledge of:
    • IIA Internal Audit Standards
    • COSO framework and risk assessment methodologies
    • Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)

This position is based at ALSAC’s National Executive Office in Memphis, TN and is eligible for a hybrid work schedule.

Job Description

As the Engineering Manager of Information Architecture, you will be responsible for delivering business value by defining, organizing, and governing information through best practices in enterprise information modeling, taxonomy, metadata management, and content labeling.

This role offers an opportunity to combine a passion for data with the discipline of information architecture to support strategic initiatives focused on donor engagement, personalization, and capacity-to-give insights. You will work closely with business and technology stakeholders to advance strategic data initiatives, foster cross-functional collaboration, promote innovation in knowledge management and advanced analytics, and provide leadership in information management, agile data governance, and modern data security and protection practices.

Essential Job Functions:

  • Leads and develops technical teams responsible for supporting information architecture and related software platforms. Establishes and promotes best practices, standards, and processes for application design, development, testing, deployment, maintenance, and documentation. Mentors Software Engineers, Business Analysts, Systems Analysts, and other team members across multiple product teams while ensuring alignment with organizational quality and information security standards.
  • Partners with the Director, Platform to develop and implement technical strategies and operational plans, including recommendations related to annual budget requirements.
  • Ensures team effectiveness through coaching, code reviews, feedback sessions, and performance management activities. Facilitates conflict resolution and supports a collaborative, high-performing work environment.
  • Champions best practices and drives the delivery of high-quality, secure, and scalable solutions. Advocates for the use of common assets, modern design principles, and framework components while providing ongoing coaching, development, and performance feedback to team members.
  • Manages vendor relationships to ensure development initiatives are delivered on time, within scope, and in accordance with organizational software engineering standards.
  • Oversees employee career development and succession planning, including the creation of growth plans and approval of education and training opportunities. Manages training-related budgets and resources.
  • Collaborates effectively with ITS departments and business stakeholders to ensure technical solutions and information architecture strategies align with organizational objectives.

Job Requirements:

  • Six (6) years of experience in information and/or data architecture, including strategy development, planning, and delivery oversight. Strong understanding of enterprise information architecture principles, including information modeling, metadata management, taxonomy, content labeling, master data management, and integration design or 4 years of experience in information or data architecture with an advanced degree.
  • Experience across multiple architectural disciplines, including Data Lake and Data Warehouse design and configuration, business and technology domains, applications, and enterprise architecture.
  • Experience working in large, complex, heterogeneous environments, including legacy platforms preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience with modern data architecture technologies and environments, including cloud platforms, Hadoop, NoSQL, and data virtualization solutions.
  • Strong analytical skills with experience leveraging reporting, analytics, and data insights to support business objectives and user experiences. Demonstrated ability to apply architectural principles to solve business challenges and drive organizational value.
  • Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
  • Experience working with data warehouse technologies, including SQL Server (preferred), Amazon Redshift, and other modern database platforms.
  • Experience with database architecture, design, and operational processes.
  • Experience with business intelligence and analytics tools such as Tableau and Unica.
  • Experience leading and developing technical and engineering teams in a collaborative, cross-functional environment.

This position is based at ALSAC’s National Executive Office in Memphis, TN and is eligible for a hybrid work schedule.

Job Description

As a Digital Experimentation Strategist, you will serve as the organization's subject matter expert for digital experimentation and decision science. In this role, you will lead the end-to-end experimentation process, including identifying and sizing opportunities, helping teams define key decisions, selecting success metrics and testing methodologies, and translating results into actionable recommendations and future testing roadmaps. You will oversee the design, execution, and analysis of digital experiments aimed at optimizing donor and supporter engagement and conversion across digital channels and platforms. Additionally, you will establish and lead the governance, training, processes, and support needed to foster a culture of experimentation and data-driven decision-making throughout the organization.

Essential Job Functions

  • Serve as the digital experimentation subject matter expert (SME) for the organization, leading decision science training, processes, and implementation.

  • Identify learning needs and serve as an educator and trainer in helping internal users understand and apply statistical methodologies and experimentation best practices more effectively and consistently.

  • Serve as the day-to-day lead of the experimentation tools and technology, partnering with Product to identify and champion new capabilities and enhancements, best practices and use cases in support of testing velocity and validity.

  • Lead the experimentation processes of defining, hypothesizing, testing, evaluating, reporting, and implementing digital experiments.

  • Grow the understanding and application of finding insights and relationships via statistics as a part of a robust decision science practice.

  • Oversee the ongoing refinement and management of centralized resources, templates, and repositories in support of a strong experimentation practice.

  • Partner closely with product teams to collaborate in building an educational curriculum that helps internal users apply tools and techniques, continually bringing forward ideas and insights to drive value for our audiences and the business.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science, Mathematics, or related field (Master’s degree preferred) and 5+ years of direct experience strategically supporting scaled testing, experimentation, and decision science within a sizeable organization with a track record of driving stronger decisioning to achieve key business outcomes; including 3+ years of proven experience in training and governing others in experimentation methodologies OR 8+ years of direct experience without a degree.

  • Experienced in weighing pragmatism against robust measurement to design and complete experiments (e.g., A/B/n test vs. pre-post analysis, learning agenda priorities).

  • Coached and mentored junior team members, performing work through others.

  • A resourceful and driven problem solver. You enjoy and have demonstrated ability solving complex problems, drawing inferences from data, and using your analysis skills and eye for business to identify solutions.

  • You have excellent organizational skills, strong attention to detail, and ability to effectively deliver on projects supporting multiple business partners.

  • Experience conducting user research including activities such as usability testing, online surveys, focus groups, user observation and field research.

  • Applied understanding of quantitative, behavioral analysis and statistical concepts.

  • Knowledge of user interface design processes and methodology, user-centered design principles and practices.

  • Experience with Agile methodology and use of Jira to organize work.

  • Great teammate and collaborator, with deep experience partnering with cross-functional team members who come to the table with different perspectives and have a consistent record of developing creative approaches to solving problems.

Location: This position is Memphis‑preferred, though we welcome strong candidates from other U.S. locations.

Job Description

Join the mission of ALSAC/St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital as a Philanthropic Advisor, where your strategic relationship-building skills will help secure the future of lifesaving research and care. This role focuses on cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding a portfolio of planned giving donors and prospects across a designated region.

Key Responsibilities

Donor Strategy & Portfolio Management

  • Manage a portfolio of 500–1000 planned giving donors and prospects, including interim support for staff vacancies.

  • Develop personalized engagement and fundraising strategies to align with donor values and philanthropic goals.

  • Conduct in-person donor cultivation, including visits, events, and strategic outreach.

  • Plan and host at least two Donor Appreciation Luncheons annually.

Planned Giving & Gift Development

  • Identify and qualify new donors to grow the planned giving and outright gift pipeline.

  • Promote giving vehicles such as bequests, charitable gift annuities, and charitable trusts.

  • Collaborate with estate attorneys and financial advisors to fulfill donor intentions.

  • Confirm new members of the Danny Thomas – St. Jude Society through timely and strategic follow-up.

Collaboration & Leadership

  • Serve as the planned giving lead within your assigned area.

  • Partner with internal teams to facilitate gifts and enhance high-value volunteer opportunities.

  • Represent ALSAC/St. Jude at donor events, community engagements, and national conferences.

  • Identify and lead initiatives that support ALSAC’s strategic fundraising goals.

Build High-Value Corporate Partnerships

  • Develop trusted relationships with corporate decision-makers and key stakeholders.
  • Deliver customized partnership solutions aligned with business objectives and organizational priorities.
  • Leverage volunteers, internal stakeholders, and community influencers to identify and secure new opportunities.
  • Utilize research, analytics, CRM insights, and moves management strategies to maximize engagement and drive results.

Lead Complex Business Development Opportunities

  • Serve as a strategic advisor for complex corporate opportunities, including multi-stakeholder, multi-market, and non-standard partnership engagements.
  • Navigate cross-functional relationships to drive alignment, problem-solving, and successful execution.
  • Provide guidance on partnership strategy, positioning, and relationship management to maximize impact and revenue potential.

Collaborate Across the Enterprise

The Enterprise AI Architect is responsible for defining and evolving ALSAC's enterprise architecture standards for Artificial Intelligence (AI), Agentic AI, and AI-enabled applications. This role partners with technology and business teams to ensure AI solutions align with enterprise architecture principles and are scalable, secure, reliable, and maintainable.

The Enterprise AI Architect provides architecture guidance, develops reusable patterns and standards, and helps teams successfully move AI solutions from concept through production implementation. This role collaborates across stakeholders to evaluate technologies, establish best practices, and ensure AI investments support ALSAC's long-term technology strategy.

Essential Job Functions

  • Define enterprise architecture standards, reference architectures, and implementation patterns for AI, Agentic AI, and AI-enabled solutions.
  • Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, Data, Security, and business teams to evaluate AI use cases, establish success criteria, and provide guidance on architectural tradeoffs, including model selection, agent design patterns, cost considerations, and responsible AI practices.
  • Design and maintain reusable architecture patterns for AI gateways, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, agent orchestration, enterprise knowledge access, retrieval architectures, and AI platform services.
  • Establish architectural guidance for AI security, identity management, authorization, governance, compliance, and policy enforcement.
  • Support adoption of AI development lifecycle (AI-DLC) practices through architecture reviews, standards, reference implementations, and implementation guidance.
  • Define architectural approaches for AI evaluation, observability, monitoring, operational readiness, and cost management.
  • Develop reference implementations and proof-of-concept solutions that accelerate delivery and help teams scale AI capabilities into production environments.
  • Ensure AI and technology solutions align with enterprise architecture standards, strategic technology roadmaps, and long-term operational objectives.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders to gather, analyze, communicate, and validate requirements impacting ALSAC's enterprise technology environment.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise architecture, solution architecture, systems integration, software engineering, or related technology disciplines.
  • Experience designing and implementing AI, Generative AI, machine learning, or intelligent automation solutions.
  • Experience developing architecture standards, reference architectures, and technology governance practices.
  • Strong understanding of cloud platforms, application integration, enterprise security, and modern software architecture patterns.
  • Ability to communicate technical concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • 5+ years of leadership, team lead, or architecture influence experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Enterprise AI architecture expertise with Bedrock, MCP, AI Gateways, LangGraph/LangChain, RAG, and agentic AI platforms.  
  • Strong architecture and implementation experience across OpenShift/Kubernetes, and scalable AI infrastructure, including deployment, operations, and lifecycle management of long-running agents.  
  • Knowledge of large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agent frameworks, vector databases, and AI observability practices.
  • Experience with responsible AI, AI governance, security, and compliance frameworks.
  • Experience creating reusable frameworks, accelerators, and architecture guidance for enterprise technology teams.

Job Description

Capability Ownership:

Job Description

The Manager, IT Supplier Management is responsible for leading ALSAC's Information Technology supplier management function, overseeing the strategy, governance, performance, and commercial management of technology suppliers across software, SaaS, cloud, infrastructure, telecommunications, consulting, and managed services.

This role serves as a key partner to IT leadership, Finance, Procurement, Legal, Information Security, and business stakeholders to ensure supplier relationships deliver measurable business value, support organizational priorities, mitigate risk, and optimize technology investments.

The Manager will lead both strategic and operational supplier management activities, including vendor selection, RFx processes, contract negotiations, renewals, performance management, supplier governance, spend optimization, and supplier relationship management. This leader will drive the continued maturity of ALSAC's IT supplier management practices while ensuring effective execution of day-to-day supplier operations.

This position is ideal for a collaborative leader who combines strong business acumen, negotiation expertise, relationship management skills, and technology industry knowledge to deliver exceptional supplier outcomes.

What You'll Do

Strategic Supplier Leadership

  • Develop, implement, and continuously improve IT supplier management policies, standards, processes, and governance practices.
  • Drive supplier management maturity, operational efficiencies, and technology spend optimization initiatives.
  • Establish supplier performance measurement frameworks, scorecards, reporting, and supplier tiering models.
  • Evaluate market trends and supplier capabilities to support strategic technology decisions.

Vendor Relationship Management

  • Lead strategic relationships with technology suppliers, consulting partners, and service providers.
  • Conduct regular business reviews and hold suppliers accountable for contractual obligations, service levels, performance commitments, and business outcomes.
  • Manage supplier escalations, dispute resolution, and performance improvement initiatives.
  • Foster collaborative supplier partnerships while maintaining strong governance and accountability.

Contract, Sourcing & Commercial Management

  • Lead vendor evaluations, RFx activities, supplier selection processes, and contract negotiations.
  • Negotiate pricing, commercial terms, service-level agreements (SLAs), renewals, Statements of Work (SOWs), and other supplier agreements.
  • Partner with Procurement, Legal, Finance, and Information Security to ensure contracts align with organizational requirements and mitigate risk.
  • Identify opportunities to consolidate suppliers, optimize licensing, and increase purchasing leverage.

Financial & Risk Management

  • Monitor supplier spend, budgeting inputs, forecasting activities, and invoice management processes.
  • Identify cost savings, cost avoidance, and value optimization opportunities across the technology portfolio.
  • Evaluate supplier financial viability, operational performance, and market conditions to proactively mitigate risk.
  • Maintain supplier risk, performance, and spend data to support business decision-making.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate closely with IT leadership, Project Management Office, Finance, Procurement, Legal, Information Security, and business stakeholders.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor on supplier strategy, contract management, sourcing approaches, and vendor governance.
  • Support technology initiatives by ensuring supplier engagements align with organizational objectives, policies, and standards.
  • Deliver training, guidance, and best practices related to supplier management across IT.

Team Leadership

  • Provide leadership, coaching, prioritization, and development for IT Supplier Management team members.
  • Oversee execution of supplier management services and operational processes.
  • Promote a culture of accountability, customer service, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree and 6 year's experience, including managerial experience.
  • Experience developing and managing IT supplier management policies, standards, governance frameworks, and operational processes.
  • Experience managing technology suppliers across software, SaaS, cloud, telecommunications, infrastructure, consulting, and managed services.

Job Description

At the intersection of generosity and healthcare innovation, the Executive Advisor, Transformational Gifts plays a critical leadership role in advancing our most ambitious philanthropic goals. This is not a traditional frontline fundraising role, although the Executive Advisor manages a portfolio of donors.  It is a strategic, highly collaborative position focused on activating relationships with ultra-wealth net worth individuals/families, empowering leaders and aligning donor passions with institutional vision at the $10M+ giving level. As a trusted partner to executive leadership, professional advisors and relationship managers at all levels, this individual will help cultivate, shape solicit and steward some of the most significant giving opportunities in our organization’s history. 

Essential Job Duties

1.    Portfolio management:  Responsible for driving revenue through the qualification, cultivation, solicitation, closing and stewardship of 10M+ gifts, meeting or exceeding established goals. 
2.    Transformational Gift Strategy: Partner with internal teams to design, refine, and drive strategies for engaging individuals, families and foundations with the capacity and intent to make transformational gifts ($10M+), ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and impact goals. Success in this role will be measured by progressive metrics – including influence on donor strategy, movement toward transformational investment, depth of engagement, activation of internal leaders and revenue targets – reflecting the complexity and long-term nature of transformational philanthropy. 

3.    Consulting and Capacity Building: Provide strategic internal consulting to relationship managers from across the organization - regardless of title or department – who are connected to transformational prospects. This includes preparation for donor conversations, gift strategy and development, long-term relationship building and solicitation. 

4.    Executive Engagement: Collaborate with the SVP – Transformational Giving, C-Suite executives, and clinical or operational leadership from the hospital on high-stakes donor cultivation steps as needed. Help prepare and coach them for pivotal donor meetings, events and stewardship activities. 

5.    High Value Volunteer Engagement: Serve in support of advisory boards and councils. Plan meaningful engagement opportunities for virtual and on campus experiences that deepen their connection to the mission and demonstrates impact. When possible, leverage their networks thoughtfully and strategically to identify and cultivate new transformational relationships, supporting peer to peer influence and expanding the pipeline of $10M+ prospects. 

6.    Narrative & Case Co-Creation: Work cross-functionally to co-create custom proposals and transformational investment opportunities that reflect the donor’s vision, values, and desired legacy – while advancing our mission in measurable, meaningful ways. 7.    Strategic Initiatives & Campaign Leadership: Play a key role in the development and execution of high-profile philanthropic initiatives, including milestone institutional anniversaries, enterprise-wide campaigns, and research-focused funding priorities. Collaborate across departments to shape compelling campaign strategies and donor experiences that align with transformational giving principles. Serve as a thought partner in designing customized approaches for complex, time-bound opportunities that inspire significant investment and long-term commitment. 

Job Requirements

  • 10+ years’ relevant work experience and proven experience in closing and/or advising on 8- and 9- figure philanthropic conversations, ideally in healthcare, higher education, or a complex mission-driven institution. 
  • Bachelor’s degree required, advanced degree preferred.
  • Natural coach and facilitator, able to build confidence and skill in others while honoring their authentic leadership style.
  • Ability to understand and translate a wide range of in-depth research initiatives and clinical care innovations into compelling, donor centered opportunities. 
  • Comfortable working in highly matrixed environments, influencing without formal authority. 
  • Exceptional emotional intelligence and ability to hold high-trust, high-impact conversations with both internal and external stakeholders.

Responsible for specifying, monitoring, gathering, analyzing, and reporting all metrics related to Product initiatives including revenue, reach, and engagement metrics such as conversion rates, web behavior, etc. for the entire digital Product portfolio. To be successful in this role you must be able to work effectively in a fluid, fast-paced environment while maintaining good communication with management and team members and be able to mentor entry level analysts. Strong communications skills, including proven writing/editing ability a must.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

1.    Support the implementation and maintenance of Digital analytics tools (Google Analytics, Adobe Analytics, Tag Management System - DTM) for the new/existing applications.
2.    Work closely with business analysts to define implementation requirements, Functional/Tagging Specification Documents and maintain documentation through Adobe Analytics SDR (Solutions Design Reference).

4.    Develop, customize, and troubleshoot events and tags in complex environments with the use of JavaScript, XML, HTML and CSS.

Educates teams on web analytics best practices and toolsets through the development of training materials, standards documentation, and takes lead in the coordination/facilitation of regular training sessions with various analytics user groups.
9.    Identify methods to improve the digital analytics front-end implementation based on internal and external data
10.    Identify online data collection issues and work with development and product teams for resolution

Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor's Degree and 6+ year's experience.
  • Requires experience with Adobe Analytics and Digital Data domain.
  • Requires experience analyzing and developing actionable insights for digital products and experiences.
  • Strong communication skills to translate data and insights into a performance data story that will inform strategy and optimization.

  • Self-motivated with strong intellectual curiosity; comfortable working with large data sets across multiple data sources;
  • Experience in website tagging and conversion path/journey tracking, as well as, building data queries in SQL as a plus.

  • Track record of diving into data to discover hidden patterns and of conducting error/deviation analysis. Experience with statistical modelling / machine learning.

  • Working understanding of data layers and Adobe Launch or Tags, including the ability to read analytics requirements and support validation through browser developer tools. Advanced implementation coding is not required.

  • Strong analytical skills with experience using SPSS or comparable statistical analysis software.
  • Demonstrated experience translating complex research findings into clear business recommendations for senior executives.

  • Experience applying AI and machine learning solutions within research, analytics, or insight generation.

Job Description

As a Sr. Advisor Area Development at ALSAC, you manage a blended portfolio of leadership annual donors, corporate partners, high-value volunteers, event committees, and strategic fundraising initiatives throughout Southern California. The Sr. Advisor Area Development is responsible for driving revenue growth through donor cultivation, sponsorship engagement, volunteer leadership development, fundraising events, stewardship activities, and cross-functional collaboration in support of ALSAC's mission. This role supports key Southern California fundraising initiatives, including Evening of Hope and other high-value donor and volunteer engagement opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

1. Creative Visionary

In collaboration with area leadership, develop and execute iconic signature event experiences that transcend expectations, from intimate gatherings to grand galas. Provide strategic leadership for complex, high-revenue fundraising events, donor cultivation experiences, and volunteer-led initiatives. Drive recruitment, engagement, and stewardship of high-profile volunteer leaders, event committees, and corporate partners while ensuring fundraising goals are achieved.

2. Organizational Pro

Manage multiple fundraising initiatives and projects autonomously with exceptional attention to detail. Coordinate event planning, sponsorship development, volunteer management, donor engagement, and stewardship activities while balancing competing priorities and deadlines.

3. Cultivate Relationships with Purpose

Utilize your exceptional interpersonal and relationship development skills to recruit, engage, and steward corporate partners, individual donors, sponsors, committee members, and volunteer leaders. Through strategic communication, personal visits, fundraising activations, and cultivation opportunities, establish relationships that extend beyond transactions and foster long-term philanthropic investment.

4. Collaborate for Impact

Partner across enterprise functions, including Development, Marketing, Event Production, Data Strategy, Volunteer Engagement, Finance, and Philanthropic Advisory teams to execute fundraising strategies and ensure alignment with organizational goals and donor engagement best practices. Monitor KPIs, assess outcomes, and recommend strategic adjustments to maximize impact.

5. Empower Fundraising Initiatives

Leverage your fundraising expertise to inspire and empower volunteers, leadership committees, sponsors, and donors. Provide motivation, direction, training, and resources through personal visits, strategic communications, and engagement opportunities to help achieve fundraising and relationship development goals.

6. Strategize for Growth

Develop and implement innovative cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and moves management strategies that strengthen engagement and philanthropic support among leadership annual, corporate, and major donor prospects. Identify opportunities to increase revenue growth and deepen stakeholder engagement.

7. Champion Donor Relationships

Manage a blended portfolio of 75-100 leadership annual donors, corporate partners, high-value volunteers, event committee members, and donor prospects. Build, maintain, and advance relationships through strategic cultivation, stewardship, sponsorship engagement, and revenue-generating opportunities designed to increase donor retention and philanthropic investment.

8. Collaboration

Collaborate closely with Development and Philanthropic Advisory teams to strengthen donor and volunteer relationship management strategies. Ensure alignment across stewardship, financial analysis, prospect management, and fundraising initiatives to maximize organizational impact and donor experience.

9. Data-Driven Impact

Utilize donor data, engagement insights, and fundraising analytics to inform strategic decision-making, stewardship plans, and portfolio management. Leverage data systems to create personalized donor experiences and optimize fundraising outcomes.

10. Elevate Our Presence

Represent ALSAC/St. Jude Children's Research Hospital in all interactions with donors, volunteers, sponsors, corporate partners, and community stakeholders. Serve as a trusted ambassador who advances the organization's mission and reinforces its commitment to excellence.

Qualifications and Experience

Strategic Fundraising Event Leadership

  • Demonstrated experience leading complex, high-revenue fundraising events, including galas, golf tournaments, dinners, and volunteer-led initiatives generating $1M+ in annual revenue. Proven ability to oversee strategic planning, fundraising execution, sponsorship development, volunteer engagement, and revenue performance.

Compelling Communication

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to convey complex ideas clearly, build consensus, influence stakeholders, and inspire action among donors, volunteers, sponsors, and community leaders.

Relationship-Based Fundraising

  • Demonstrated success cultivating, soliciting, stewarding, and managing relationships with leadership annual donors, corporate partners, major donor prospects, and volunteer leaders. Proven ability to implement moves management strategies that drive donor engagement and revenue growth.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Project Management

  • Experience navigating multiple stakeholders and coordinating efforts across fundraising, marketing, volunteer engagement, event planning, production, finance, and other enterprise teams. Strong project management skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and maintain momentum across multiple initiatives.

Experience in Philanthropy

  • Strong background in relationship-based fundraising, committee engagement, corporate partnerships, board development, strategic planning, and execution of premier fundraising events. Experience developing donor engagement strategies and volunteer leadership programs that drive fundraising success.

Senior Leadership Presence

  • Demonstrated leadership capability with a strategic mindset focused on revenue growth, volunteer leadership development, donor engagement, sponsorship expansion, and innovative fundraising solutions.

Corporate Sector Relationships

  • Ideally possess established relationships within the corporate sector and a proven ability to identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward corporate sponsors and donors.

High-Value Volunteer Leadership

  • Proven ability to recruit, inspire, engage, and steward influential volunteer leaders, executive committees, corporate partners, boards, and community stakeholders. Experience managing complex volunteer structures and committee-driven fundraising efforts.

Regional Sales Analytics

Reporting and KPI Management

    • Demonstrable experience in parameter-efficient fine-tuning, model quantization, and quantization-aware fine-tuning of LLM models
    • Hands-on knowledge of Chain-of-Thoughts, Tree-of-Thoughts, Graph-of-Thoughts prompting strategies
